This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 1:

"Surah: an-nazalnaha... wa lahu tadhakkarun" (the opening of the Surah, "a Surah which We have sent down and made obligatory, and in which We have sent down clear signs, that you may remember").

This is the only opening of its kind in the entire Qur'an. The new word in it is "faradnaha" (We have made it obligatory). As far as I understand, its meaning is that what is contained in this Surah must be taken and acted upon. That is, acting upon the manners mentioned in it is obligatory in the same way that acting upon the hudud (prescribed punishments) is obligatory. These morals and habits are extremely natural. People forget these manners and morals because of certain temporary circumstances that deceive a person and lead him astray. These verses remind such people, show them the straight path, and then bring them back to the path of nature, which is perfectly clear.

After this unambiguous introduction, the discussion of the law of the prescribed punishment for adultery (hadd al-zina) begins. Regarding this act as extremely abominable, it is stated that the adulterer has no connection left with Islamic society.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verses 2–3 (part 1 of 2):

(Az-zaniyu ... ʿala al-mu'minin) (3)

In the early days of Islam, the punishment for adultery (zina) was that which was mentioned in the verse of Surah an-Nisa:

(Wallati ya'tina ... sabilan) (4:15) "And as for those of your women who commit obscenity, call four witnesses against them from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way."

The punishment for a woman was that she be confined in a house and be tormented through reproach. And the man too was subjected to censure and reproach.

After this, the command came in Surah an-Nur, and this was the way that Allah had opened for those who commit zina, a matter to which Allah had alluded in Surah an-Nisa.

This punishment of lashes is for those men and women who are not married, that is, those who have not been safeguarded from the commission of this crime through marriage. And this punishment is to be enforced when the offender is Muslim, adult and free. As for the one who is muhsan, that is, one who has married and, as a result of that marriage, has had intercourse with his wife, and who is Muslim, adult and free, and whose marriage is also a valid marriage according to the Shariah, his punishment is the punishment of stoning (rajm).

The punishment of stoning is established by the Sunnah, while the punishment of lashes is established by the Holy Quran. The verse of the Quran was general and unspecific. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the punishment of stoning to muhsan adulterers, and therefore it became established that the punishment of lashes is for non-muhsan.

Here there is a difference among the jurists as to whether the muhsan shall also be given lashes before stoning or not. The majority of scholars hold that the two punishments cannot be combined. Furthermore, there is also a difference of opinion as to whether, when the non-muhsan adulterer is given the punishment of lashes, he shall also be exiled according to the hadith or not; similarly there is a difference regarding the punishment of an adulterous slave. These differences require very lengthy discussions. It is appropriate that readers obtain information about them from books of jurisprudence. Here we shall speak only about the philosophy and wisdom underlying this law. You have read that the punishment of virgins is limited to lashes, and the punishment of married muhsanin is stoning. This is because a person who, being Muslim, adult and free, has had intercourse with a woman within a valid marriage, has come to know and have access to the pure, honourable and decent way. If such a person adopts sexual licentiousness, it becomes evident that a natural corruption has arisen within him. Such a person has deviated from the path of nature and the path of Islam, and therefore he should receive the harshest of punishments. As for the unmarried non-muhsan, the possibility of error occurring from them is greater, because at times they may be overcome by the intensity of passion, while they are still in the age of ignorance. Furthermore, there is also a difference in the crime itself: the muhsan, since he has prior experience in this act, benefits more from this act compared to the virgin, who is not so experienced.

The Quran here mentions only the punishment of the non-muhsan, that is, virgins, as we have made clear, and here emphasis is laid on not showing any leniency to anyone in this matter.

(Az-zaniyatu ... al-mu'minin) (24:2) "The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes. And let not compassion for them in the religion of Allah seize you, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day; and let a group of the believers witness their punishment."

The command is that the enforcement of the Islamic prescribed punishments be carried out strictly, and that no concession, leniency or mercy be shown in this matter, because this matter concerns the religion of Allah, and leniency in matters of religion is intolerable. Moreover, at the time of the enforcement of the punishment, a number of believers should be present so that the effect of the punishment on the offender is greater; so that he is tormented also spiritually, and so that it serves as a lesson for the onlookers.

After this, in order to show the disapproval and abhorrence of this act, the perpetrators of this act are separated from Islamic social life, that is, this act is so repugnant that no person should marry such offenders.

(Az-zani ... ʿala al-mu'minin) (24:3) "The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or an idolatress, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or an idolater. And that has been made unlawful for the believers."

Thus it is understood that when someone commits this evil act, he does not commit it while he is a believer. Those who commit this crime are in such a psychological state that at that time faith departs from their consciousness and heart, and after the commission of this act it is not permissible for any believing soul to marry a person who has left the circle of faith because of this vile act. A believer detests such a relationship and his conscience recoils from it, to the extent that Imam Ahmad (rahimahullah) regards marriage between an adulterer and a chaste woman as unlawful. Likewise, he regards marriage between a chaste man and an adulteress as unlawful as well, unless the two are cleansed through repentance and this filth is removed. In any case, a chaste believing woman refuses to marry an adulterer, and likewise a chaste believing man regards marriage to an adulteress as abhorrent. Since the word "haram" has been used for this kind of marriage, the Shariah and religious temperament nonetheless regard it as abominable.

(Wa-hurrima dhalika ʿala al-mu'minin) (24:3) "And that has been made unlawful for the believers." Thus the impure and filthy people are separated from Islamic society.

It is narrated in the occasion of revelation of this verse that a man, Murthid ibn Abi Murthid, used to carry weak captives from Makkah to Madinah ("those whom the people of Makkah had prevented from migrating to Madinah"). In Makkah there was a debauched woman named ʿAnaq, who was a friend of Murthid. Murthid had fixed a time with one of the detained captives in Makkah that he would take him away at night. They say it was a moonlit night, and I was in the shadow of a house wall in Makkah. ʿAnaq came and saw the shadow adjoining the wall. When she came to me, she recognised me and said, "Are you Murthid?" I said, "I am Murthid." She said, "Welcome, you are welcome, come and stay with us tonight." I said to her, "ʿAnaq! Allah has made zina unlawful." She raised an uproar in the area, saying, "Look, Murthid is taking away your prisoners." So I entered a garden and eight men followed me. I reached a cave or a hollow and entered it. They came and stood over my head and urinated. Their urine was falling on my head, but Allah had made them so blind that they did not see me. Murthid says that these people returned, and I too came back and took my companion. He was a very cunning man. I reached Idhkhir, I untied his ropes, I lifted him and he too helped me, until we reached Madinah. I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and requested him: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish to marry ʿAnaq." I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) this question twice, and he gave me no answer. Then this verse was revealed:

(Az-zani ... ʿala al-mu'minin) (24:3) "The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or an idolatress, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or an idolater. And that has been made unlawful for the believers."

Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Murthid, the adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or an idolatress; so do not marry her." (Abu Dawud, Nasai, Tirmidhi).

This narration shows that marriage of a believer to an adulteress is not permissible until she repents. Likewise, no believing woman may marry an adulterer unless he repents. This is the opinion of Imam Ahmad. Other jurists have adopted other views. This issue is a matter of difference, and details can be seen in books of jurisprudence. In any case, zina is an act by which its perpetrator is no longer fit to remain in Islamic society. He should be removed from Islamic society and be removed. This too is a kind of punishment for such offenders, just as the punishment of lashes is a punishment.

Islam has prescribed such severe and decisive punishment for this abominable and repugnant act. This is not because Islam wishes to wage some war against the natural requirements of man. Islam indeed accepts that man should have arrangements for fulfilling his natural inclinations and natural requirements. Islam does not see human welfare in uprooting man's natural inclinations root and branch. Nor is Islam opposed to the natural impulses that the Creator of the universe has placed within the nature of man, and these are part of the great laws of life of this universe. Through these natural inclinations the continuity of the chain of life is maintained, and the secret of the construction and development of the earth also lies in them, which is part of the duty of vicegerency on earth. Indeed, the struggle of the Islamic system of life is in reality a struggle against animality. For an animal there is no distinction between one body and another body. Animals have no family, no common dwelling place, and no shared life; there is only a physical union for a few moments. Islam does not wish to base human life on such temporary inclinations; rather, Islam establishes sexual relations on the basis of advanced human consciousness, that "pure and refined bodies should join with one another, two hearts and two souls should come together, two human beings should unite, a shared life should be built between them, they should have shared hopes, shared sorrow and pain, a shared future, and they should have children. They should share in each other's joys and responsibilities, and this new coming generation should grow up in one common dwelling place, and both parents should stand to guard and nurture this nursery."

This is why Islam has adopted such severity in the punishment for zina, because in sexual relations zina is equivalent to falling to the level of animality. It negates all the high values that Islam holds in view, and all the social aims that Islam seeks to bring into operation are lost. Through it a human being falls merely to the level of animality, because if there is no distinction between woman and woman and no distinction is made between man and man, this is the animal level. Under a system of free lust, humanity is so distorted that people sacrifice everything for a momentary hunger of flesh and blood. And from this temporary and animal sexual union, there is no impulse to build life, no plan to construct this earth, nor any desire to obtain offspring through it; rather, behind it there is no real and lofty impulse at all. For love and inclination should also have a kind of permanence, whereas whatever lies behind zina is entirely temporary. In some societies, although there are long-lasting relations of friendship and love, behind them there are no high human values; behind them there is only animality.

As far as Islam is concerned, it neither suppresses natural inclinations and desires nor considers them an impure thing. Islam organises and regulates them and grants them purity, and by raising them above the animal level it makes them an institution and a centre around which countless psychological and social etiquettes gather. As for zina, and especially prostitution, these natural emotions become devoid of purity, spirituality and lofty desires. Moreover, the etiquettes and values that have always been associated with this institution in the history of the human race are stripped away from it, and it falls to mere animal sensuality, indeed becoming more filthy, dirty and degraded than an animal, because there are countless animals and birds that live together and have an organised marital life, and in that life there is no chaos in sexual relations, as there is between two human adulterers, and especially in the case of prostitute women, where both parties are lower than animals.

Since Islam wishes to remove this degradation from human society, it has therefore adopted such severity in the punishment for zina. Scholars have mentioned some other reasons against the crime of zina, and each of them too provides a complete justification for imposing such a severe punishment for zina, for example that it causes confusion of lineage, produces hatred, rancour and enmity among people, and disturbs the peace of settled households, and so on. But in my view the real and comprehensive cause of this punishment is that man should be elevated above the pit of animal sexual union, and that the values and etiquettes that have always been associated with the human institution of sexual union should be preserved, and that this institution should be given permanence, so that spouses live a shared life for the sake of high values and high purposes. This is the most important and all-encompassing reason, the cause that encompasses all the reasons.

Moreover, it is also a fact that Islam adopts severity in punishing this crime only when all the preventive and deterrent measures against the occurrence of this crime have been adopted. Islam is a complete system of life, and when it is established, society has been organised along such lines that there are abundant opportunities for living a pure life and limited opportunities for living a base and filthy life. Then Islam enforces this punishment upon those who, abandoning pure ways, adopt filthy ways. And in this situation there are several examples and instances that confirm what we have said.

Furthermore, even if this crime does occur, Islam has laid down such a difficult procedure for its proof that some doubt almost always arises in one form or another. And in the criminal law of Islam, the important principle has been established that the accusation of crime is dropped on account of doubts. Hadrat Aishah (RA) narrates that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Remove the hudud (prescribed punishments) from the Muslims as far as you can. If there is any way for the accused to be released, let him go, for it is better for the judge to err in pardoning than to err in punishing." This is why Islam requires four witnesses who are also upright (ʿadl), and who testify that they saw the act with their own eyes, or else a confession from the accused that contains no doubt.

Sometimes it is objected that if Islam imposes the condition of four witnesses, then this punishment becomes a punishment in theory only, and there would be no possibility of its implementation. But, as we mentioned above, Islam does not eliminate the crime of adultery from Islamic society through punishment alone; the Islamic system also adopts other preventive measures, due to which this crime actually occurs much less often. Islam emphasizes the refinement and training of the human being. It purifies the human conscience. Islam creates within people the fear that whoever commits this crime, if his crime is exposed, will become known in that society as a person of bad character; no one will give him his daughter in marriage, or no one will take his daughter as a wife. He will be cut off from Islamic society. Islam imposes punishment only on those who commit this crime so brazenly that four persons see them, or it imposes this punishment on those who fear God and who wish to purify themselves through punishment, and who confess their crime, as happened with Hadrat Maiz and Ghamidiyyah. Both came themselves to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, purify us." They insisted on this, although the Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from the matter four times, and after they had insisted and confessed four times, he ordered that the hadd be carried out. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Pardon hudud among yourselves; if a matter of hudud reaches me, its enforcement becomes obligatory." (Abu Dawud).

But when certainty of the commission of the crime has been established and the matter has reached the competent authorities, then no leniency is permitted in it. Then the enforcement of the hudud becomes obligatory, and it becomes a matter of religion, and showing mercy in it is not permissible. Showing mercy after the proof of the crime means showing mercy to the criminal while being cruel to society, and oppressing human decency and the human conscience. This would in reality be a false mercy. Compared with us, Allah is more merciful to His servants, and Allah has prescribed this punishment, and no believing man or believing woman has the choice, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice of their own in it. Allah is well aware of the interests of His servants. Moreover, Allah knows the temperaments of His servants better than we do, so no one who speaks should be permitted to say that a particular punishment is harsh. We say that compared with the spread of this shameful crime in society, it is a very mild punishment, because when this crime spreads, society falls into afflictions such as decline, backwardness, corruption of nature, and shamelessness.

It is not only through severity in the punishment for adultery that the Islamic society is meant to be protected, nor does the Islamic system rely only on punishments to keep the Islamic community pure and clean. As we have explained, Islam takes other steps to protect society from this crime. Islam prohibits all those acts which even carry a whiff of this crime.

This is why the adulterers are removed from the body of the Muslim Ummah. The next step taken is that making an accusation of adultery against chaste women has also been declared a crime, unless someone produces four witnesses. This is so that people do not become bold in leveling the accusation of this shameful crime.

Islam imposes punishment only on those who commit this crime so brazenly that four persons see them, or it imposes this punishment on those who fear God and who wish to purify themselves through punishment, and who confess their crime, as happened with Hadrat Maiz and Ghamidiyyah. Both came themselves to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, purify us." They insisted on this, although the Prophet (ﷺ) turned away from the matter four times, and after they had insisted and confessed four times, he ordered that the hadd be carried out. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Pardon hudud among yourselves; if a matter of hudud reaches me, its enforcement becomes obligatory." (Abu Dawud).

But when certainty of the commission of the crime has been established and the matter has reached the competent authorities, then no leniency is permitted in it. Then the enforcement of the hudud becomes obligatory, and it becomes a matter of religion, and showing mercy in it is not permissible. Showing mercy after the proof of the crime means showing mercy to the criminal while being cruel to society, and oppressing human decency and the human conscience. This would in reality be a false mercy. Compared with us, Allah is more merciful to His servants, and Allah has prescribed this punishment, and no believing man or believing woman has the choice, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice of their own in it. Allah is well aware of the interests of His servants. Moreover, Allah knows the temperaments of His servants better than we do, so no one who speaks should be permitted to say that a particular punishment is harsh. We say that compared with the spread of this shameful crime in society, it is a very mild punishment, because when this crime spreads, society falls into afflictions such as decline, backwardness, corruption of nature, and shamelessness.

It is not only through severity in the punishment for adultery that the Islamic society is meant to be protected, nor does the Islamic system rely only on punishments to keep the Islamic community pure and clean. As we have explained, Islam takes other steps to protect society from this crime. Islam prohibits all those acts which even carry a whiff of this crime.

This is why the adulterers are removed from the body of the Muslim Ummah. The next step taken is that making an accusation of adultery against chaste women has also been declared a crime, unless someone produces four witnesses. This is so that people do not become bold in leveling the accusation of this shameful crime.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 4:

(Those who... ...they are the defiantly disobedient.) (4)

To let the tongue loose so that it hurls accusations against chaste women (muhsanat). Muhsanat are the virgin and married women against whom the crime of fornication (zina) is alleged, but for which there is no conclusive proof behind the accusation. That is, without any evidence, someone goes about accusing an innocent man or woman of that foul crime, and there is no one to call him to account for it. In this way, morning and evening, people's honour is attacked in society, society is defamed, and there are constant opportunities for everyone to be accused. Or a husband may suspect his wife. Everyone may come to doubt the lineage of his own descent. There is the risk of every family breaking apart. These will be the conditions of slander, accusation and suspicion in which no person will feel any security.

Then, if accusations of fornication continue to be made in this manner, ordinary people will gain the courage to commit this crime. People will say that this crime is spreading everywhere in society. In this way, even a person who wishes to avoid it will become involved in it. At the very least, because of repeated accusations, the commission of this act will not remain so abhorrent in people's minds. An ordinary person will also get the impression that ordinary people commit this crime.

If the accusation of zina without proof is not declared an offence, then even the severe punishment for zina will be of no benefit, the atmosphere of the whole society will be steeped in this crime, and the incidence of immorality will increase.

For these reasons, in order to protect people from unjust slander, and to protect people's honour from such accusations, the Qur'an has been severe in the punishment for qadhf (false accusation). It has been so severe that it has declared its punishment almost equal to the punishment for committing the crime itself, namely eighty lashes. Along with this, it has also been decided that such a person shall be deemed a fasiq (defiantly disobedient), and his testimony shall never be accepted thereafter. The first punishment, namely the eighty lashes, is a physical punishment; the second is a punishment that diminishes his standing, so that in society the word of the one who accuses someone of zina becomes worthless, and no one will trust anything he says in future. The third is also a religious punishment, in that he has strayed from the straight path of Islam, unless he produces four witnesses, or three witnesses who are with him if he himself has seen it. At that time, his statement will be considered correct and the accused will again be subject to the punishment for zina.

As far as the priorities of Islamic society are concerned, if an accusation that has no proof behind it is suppressed, then there will be no loss in such a case, whereas the loss would be considerable if immorality became widely talked about and there was no proof of it. Because in that case many people may become ready to commit that vile crime, whereas generally they used to refrain from it, and they understood that it is a most forbidden act and its commission is wrong. As for what happens to chaste women because of this accusation, and the unrest that spreads in society and the way households are destroyed, this is a common matter, and every decent person understands it well. In short, the sword of disgrace is constantly hanging over the head of the one who makes the accusation (qadhif). Except that:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 5:

(Except those who...... forgiving, merciful) (5)

Among the jurists there is a difference of opinion regarding this exception: whether it relates only to the punishment in the Hereafter, meaning that the attribute of fisq (transgression) is removed from that person but he remains disqualified from giving testimony as before, or whether his testimony is also accepted after repentance. Imam Ahmad and Imam al-Shafi'i hold the view that if he repents, his testimony will be accepted, because the ruling of fisq has been lifted. Imam Abu Hanifa says that the exception applies only to the final clause, meaning that fisq will be lifted, but this person will remain disqualified from giving testimony as before. Al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak have also adopted the opinion that his testimony is not to be accepted even if he repents, until he confesses against himself that he had lied. After that, his testimony is accepted.

In my view, the position of al-Dahhak and al-Sha'bi is more sound, because in that case the person who was accused is, in social terms, directly declared free of the accusation. In this way all the effects of qadhf (slander) are eliminated. Then no one will say that the qadhf-penalty was imposed on the accuser because he did not produce testimony, nor will anyone have the bad thought that the accusation may have been true but the accuser could not find witnesses. In this way the honour of the person accused is also restored, and the accuser's social standing is also restored through repentance. Thus all the consequences of that earlier case are removed. Now there is no justification for the testimony of the accuser to remain unaccepted even after repentance, when he has also admitted his false accusation and reformed himself through repentance.

This has been the case of a general accusation of zina. As for an accusation between spouses, that is a separate matter: if a husband accuses his wife of zina, he would be required to produce four witnesses, which would be a very great hardship. Therefore, the Shari'ah has presumed that a husband cannot falsely accuse his own wife, since his own honour and dignity are at stake in it. Hence, the Shari'ah has prescribed a special procedure for such an accusation, called li'an.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verses 6–10:

والذین یرمون۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ وان اللہ تواب حکیم ) (6 تا 10) ” “۔

In these verses, a measure of ease has been provided within the law of hadd al-qadhf (the prescribed punishment for slander) for spouses, and this ease is more suitable for the delicate relationship between husband and wife. If the husband comes to know that his wife has committed adultery, and the only witness to this is himself, then the procedure in this case is that he swears four times, by Allah, that his claim is true, that is, the accusation of adultery, and for the fifth time he says that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is lying. This testimony has been called shahadat (testimony) because it is a number of testimonies from a single witness. If the husband does this, he shall pay the mahr (dower), and a talaq ba'in (irrevocable divorce) takes effect upon the woman. And the hadd of adultery, that is rajm (stoning), is to be enforced upon her. However, if the woman wishes to have this punishment waived from herself, then against the previous testimony she swears four times that the accuser is ... and for the fifth time she swears that the wrath of Allah be upon her if she is lying. In this way the hadd is dropped from her. And through li'an she is separated from her husband. The child's lineage shall not be attached to the father if she is pregnant; rather, the child's lineage is to the mother, and an accusation of illegitimacy against a child of this kind is subject to the hadd of qadhf.

Following this, there comes this conclusion and commentary.

(ولولا۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ تواب حکیم) (24 : 10) "Were it not for the grace and mercy of Allah upon you, and were it not that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise, (the matter of accusations against your wives would have placed you in great difficulty)." Here Allah has not explained what would have happened had the grace of Allah not been there? Allah left it vague so that people would remain fearful of it. The verse indicates that it would have been some great evil, but Allah averted it.

In this context, some authentic hadiths report the occasion of revelation of this legislation. Imam Ahmad narrated from Hadrat Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) that when this verse was revealed:

(والذین۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ ابدا) (24 : 4) "And those who accuse chaste women and then do not bring four witnesses, lash them with eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony."

Sa'd ibn Ubadah (رضي الله عنه), who was the chief of the Ansar, said: "Is this verse revealed in this manner?" Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief is saying?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him; he is a very jealous man. He has never married any woman except a virgin, and when he divorced a woman, no one dared to marry her because of his jealousy." Then Sa'd (رضي الله عنه) said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the reality is that I know this is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am astonished that if a man should place his thigh upon my wife's thigh, I should not be permitted to disturb him or move him from his place until I bring four witnesses. By Allah, by the time I bring four witnesses he will have finished his work and gone away."

It is said that not much time had passed when Hilal ibn Umayyah came. He had returned from his land after work at the time of 'Isha. He saw a man with his wife. He saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears, so he did not disturb that man. In the morning, as soon as it was day, he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger, I came home at 'Isha time at night and saw a man with my wife. I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greatly disliked this report from that man. This was very burdensome for the Prophet (ﷺ), but the Ansar gathered together and said: "What Sa'd ibn Ubadah said was a great trial for us. Now the situation has reached the point that the Prophet (ﷺ) will flog Hilal ibn Umayyah and his testimony will be forever unacceptable among the people." Then Hilal ibn Umayyah said: "By Allah, I hope that Allah will surely create a way out of this for me." Hilal said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, I know how much displeasure your words have caused you, but Allah knows that I am truthful." By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was just about to order the enforcement of the hadd of qadhf upon Hilal ibn Umayyah when suddenly revelation came. When revelation came upon the Prophet (ﷺ), the Companions would immediately understand that the descent of revelation had begun. All the Companions would withdraw from the Prophet (ﷺ) until the process of revelation was complete. Then this verse was revealed:

(والذین یرمون۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ شھدت باللہ) (24 : 7) "And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them (is that) he swear four times by Allah that he is truthful in his accusation."

When the state of revelation passed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Hilal, rejoice! Allah has made ease for you and created a way out of this difficulty." Hilal said: "I was hoping that Allah would create a way out for me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then ordered that the woman be called. She came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited these verses to both of them, admonished them, and told them that the punishment of this world is very little compared with the punishment of the Hereafter. Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have spoken the truth about her," and the woman replied: "He is lying." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make li'an between the two of them." So Hilal was told: "Testify four times that you are speaking the truth." When he was about to give the fifth testimony, he was told: "Fear Allah; the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this testimony, which makes punishment obligatory for the opposing party, will be a cause of punishment for you." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will never punish me for this, just as He did not punish me with the lashes." So for the fifth time Hilal testified that if she was lying, the curse of Allah be upon her. After this the woman was told to give four testimonies that he was lying, and for the fifth time she was told: "Fear Allah; the punishment of this world is very light compared with the punishment of the Hereafter, and this fifth testimony makes punishment obligatory and will make it obligatory upon you." She hesitated for a while and decided to confess. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people." So she gave the fifth testimony that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was truthful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated the two of them and decided that the child should not be attributed to the father, nor should the child be accused. Whoever called the child illegitimate, the hadd would be enforced upon him. He also ordered that it would not be obligatory for the husband to provide the woman with a residence or maintenance, because the two had been separated without a divorce. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that if her child turned out to be reddish-haired, thin-buttocked and thin-legged, then he would be Hilal's child; and if he turned out to be wheat-complexioned, with curly hair, large limbs, thick calves and full buttocks, then he would be the son of the man with whom she had been defamed. When her child was born, he was somewhat curly-haired, with large limbs, thick legs and full buttocks. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for the oath, I would have dealt with this woman." 

This was the law of li'an, and it was revealed to address a practical necessity. It resolved a difficult problem faced by the Muslims. This problem was so difficult that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself saw no solution to it, as is reported in Bukhari. He told Hilal ibn Umayyah: either bring witnesses, or the hadd will be enforced on your back. And Hilal kept saying: "O Messenger of Allah, if a man sees another man on his wife, will he go off to look for witnesses?"

Here, the questioner may ask: did Allah not know that after the general law of qadhf, this kind of problem would arise? Why did He not reveal this exception first, and why did Allah allow such a difficulty to arise?

The answer is that, certainly, Allah knew, but Allah, in His wisdom of legislation, decreed that the law be revealed when the need for it was felt among the people, so that they would accept it with great eagerness and fully understand the wisdom contained in the law. This is why this commentary came after it:

(ولولا۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ حکیم) (24 : 10) "Had it not been for the grace and mercy of Allah, and were it not that Allah is Most Relenting, All-Wise..."

Now consider this event carefully. See how Islam was functioning, how the training of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was working and how effective it was, and how through this Qur'an a completely new society was being built. Islam had trained a jealous people like the Arabs. It had transformed them completely. These people were so jealous and emotional that the law of hadd al-qadhf was revealed. For these emotional people this is an extremely difficult law. Once they were provoked, they were ready to do the greatest deeds. For them this is extremely burdensome, so burdensome that Hadrat Sa'd ibn Ubadah asks the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whether this law was indeed revealed in this manner. He asks questions, yet he knows that the law has indeed been revealed. Through this question he expresses the difficulty he feels, of how he would bear it if such a situation arose in his own house. He expresses this bitter reality by saying: "O Messenger of Allah, I know that this is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am astonished that if I saw a man placing his thigh upon the thigh of my wife, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him from his place until I brought four witnesses. By Allah, by the time I bring four witnesses he will have completed his task."

This was Sa'd ibn Ubadah's intellectual notion and thought. But a particular person, with his own ears and eyes, sees that this immorality is being done with his wife, and he holds back, and indeed the Qur'an has restrained him. This man controls his feelings, his thirst for revenge, his fierce Arab jealousy, the sudden surge of blood and the uncontrollable movement of his nerves. He exercises an unbreakable self-control which one cannot even imagine in Arab society. He comes helplessly and awaits the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Although this matter is extremely burdensome for him, the Qur'an had so trained these people that this man fully controls this storm of emotion, so that the command that is obeyed is the one that comes from Allah, both in his soul and in all the affairs of his person.

How was this training possible? It happened because they had complete certainty that Allah was with them, and that they were under Allah's watch and protection. Allah takes care of them and does not place them in a calamity they cannot bear, and does not leave them in difficulties that are unbearable for them. Allah never wrongs human beings. These people always lived under Allah's shade. They were breathing in an atmosphere of Allah's mercy and kindness. They were constantly looking towards Allah in the way a child looks towards his merciful and generous father. Hilal ibn Umayyah saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears. He was alone. He complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found no provision in the law except the enforcement of the hadd of qadhf. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) even announced that it was either testimony or the hadd on his back, but Hilal ibn Umayyah had the certainty that Allah would not leave him unsupported in such circumstances, since he was indeed truthful. Thus this exception came from Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave Hilal ibn Umayyah the good news, and he repeated his assurance, saying: "I had this hope from my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic." These people had complete assurance that they were under Allah's supervision, that Allah was watching, and that they had not been left to themselves to settle matters on their own. They were before Allah, in His court. This is true faith, obedience and submission and contentment, which was the distinguishing quality of the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Now the context moves beyond the middle of the law of hadd al-qadhf, and another glimpse of the vileness of the crime of qadhf is shown. Its connection is with the household of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The honour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself is at stake in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the most honoured servant of Allah. Then in this incident the honour of Hadrat Siddiq (رضي الله عنه) is also at stake, who is the most honoured person among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). Then there is also the matter of the honour of another Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal (رضي الله عنه). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself testifies that he knew nothing of Safwan except good. This incident is one in which the Muslims of Madinah remained in extreme distress for a month.

If the husband comes to know that his wife has committed adultery, and the only witness to this is himself, then the procedure in this case is that he swears four times, by Allah, that his claim is true, that is, the accusation of adultery, and for the fifth time he says that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is lying. This testimony has been called shahadat (testimony) because it is a number of testimonies from a single witness. If the husband does this, he shall pay the mahr (dower), and a talaq ba'in (irrevocable divorce) takes effect upon the woman. And the hadd of adultery, that is rajm (stoning), is to be enforced upon her. However, if the woman wishes to have this punishment waived from herself, then against the previous testimony she swears four times that the accuser is ... and for the fifth time she swears that the wrath of Allah be upon her if she is lying. In this way the hadd is dropped from her. And through li'an she is separated from her husband. The child's lineage shall not be attached to the father if she is pregnant; rather, the child's lineage is to the mother, and an accusation of illegitimacy against a child of this kind is subject to the hadd of qadhf.

Following this, there comes this conclusion and commentary.

(ولولا۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ تواب حکیم) (24 : 10) "Were it not for the grace and mercy of Allah upon you, and were it not that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise, (the matter of accusations against your wives would have placed you in great difficulty)." Here Allah has not explained what would have happened had the grace of Allah not been there? Allah left it vague so that people would remain fearful of it. The verse indicates that it would have been some great evil, but Allah averted it.

In this context, some authentic hadiths report the occasion of revelation of this legislation. Imam Ahmad narrated from Hadrat Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) that when this verse was revealed:

(والذین۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ ابدا) (24 : 4) "And those who accuse chaste women and then do not bring four witnesses, lash them with eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony."

Sa'd ibn Ubadah (رضي الله عنه), who was the chief of the Ansar, said: "Is this verse revealed in this manner?" Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief is saying?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him; he is a very jealous man. He has never married any woman except a virgin, and when he divorced a woman, no one dared to marry her because of his jealousy." Then Sa'd (رضي الله عنه) said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the reality is that I know this is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am astonished that if a man should place his thigh upon my wife's thigh, I should not be permitted to disturb him or move him from his place until I bring four witnesses. By Allah, by the time I bring four witnesses he will have finished his work and gone away."

It is said that not much time had passed when Hilal ibn Umayyah came. He had returned from his land after work at the time of 'Isha. He saw a man with his wife. He saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears, so he did not disturb that man. In the morning, as soon as it was day, he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger, I came home at 'Isha time at night and saw a man with my wife. I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greatly disliked this report from that man. This was very burdensome for the Prophet (ﷺ), but the Ansar gathered together and said: "What Sa'd ibn Ubadah said was a great trial for us. Now the situation has reached the point that the Prophet (ﷺ) will flog Hilal ibn Umayyah and his testimony will be forever unacceptable among the people." Then Hilal ibn Umayyah said: "By Allah, I hope that Allah will surely create a way out of this for me." Hilal said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, I know how much displeasure your words have caused you, but Allah knows that I am truthful." By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was just about to order the enforcement of the hadd of qadhf upon Hilal ibn Umayyah when suddenly revelation came. When revelation came upon the Prophet (ﷺ), the Companions would immediately understand that the descent of revelation had begun. All the Companions would withdraw from the Prophet (ﷺ) until the process of revelation was complete. Then this verse was revealed:

(والذین یرمون۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ شھدت باللہ) (24 : 7) "And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them (is that) he swear four times by Allah that he is truthful in his accusation."

When the state of revelation passed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Hilal, rejoice! Allah has made ease for you and created a way out of this difficulty." Hilal said: "I was hoping that Allah would create a way out for me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then ordered that the woman be called. She came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited these verses to both of them, admonished them, and told them that the punishment of this world is very little compared with the punishment of the Hereafter. Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have spoken the truth about her," and the woman replied: "He is lying." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make li'an between the two of them." So Hilal was told: "Testify four times that you are speaking the truth." When he was about to give the fifth testimony, he was told: "Fear Allah; the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this testimony, which makes punishment obligatory for the opposing party, will be a cause of punishment for you." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will never punish me for this, just as He did not punish me with the lashes." So for the fifth time Hilal testified that if she was lying, the curse of Allah be upon her. After this the woman was told to give four testimonies that he was lying, and for the fifth time she was told: "Fear Allah; the punishment of this world is very light compared with the punishment of the Hereafter, and this fifth testimony makes punishment obligatory and will make it obligatory upon you." She hesitated for a while and decided to confess. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people." So she gave the fifth testimony that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was truthful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated the two of them and decided that the child should not be attributed to the father, nor should the child be accused. Whoever called the child illegitimate, the hadd would be enforced upon him. He also ordered that it would not be obligatory for the husband to provide the woman with a residence or maintenance, because the two had been separated without a divorce. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that if her child turned out to be reddish-haired, thin-buttocked and thin-legged, then he would be Hilal's child; and if he turned out to be wheat-complexioned, with curly hair, large limbs, thick calves and full buttocks, then he would be the son of the man with whom she had been defamed. When her child was born, he was somewhat curly-haired, with large limbs, thick legs and full buttocks. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for the oath, I would have dealt with this woman." 

This was the law of li'an, and it was revealed to address a practical necessity. It resolved a difficult problem faced by the Muslims. This problem was so difficult that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself saw no solution to it, as is reported in Bukhari. He told Hilal ibn Umayyah: either bring witnesses, or the hadd will be enforced on your back. And Hilal kept saying: "O Messenger of Allah, if a man sees another man on his wife, will he go off to look for witnesses?"

Here, the questioner may ask: did Allah not know that after the general law of qadhf, this kind of problem would arise? Why did He not reveal this exception first, and why did Allah allow such a difficulty to arise?

The answer is that, certainly, Allah knew, but Allah, in His wisdom of legislation, decreed that the law be revealed when the need for it was felt among the people, so that they would accept it with great eagerness and fully understand the wisdom contained in the law. This is why this commentary came after it:

(ولولا۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ حکیم) (24 : 10) "Had it not been for the grace and mercy of Allah, and were it not that Allah is Most Relenting, All-Wise..."

Now consider this event carefully. See how Islam was functioning, how the training of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was working and how effective it was, and how through this Qur'an a completely new society was being built. Islam had trained a jealous people like the Arabs. It had transformed them completely. These people were so jealous and emotional that the law of hadd al-qadhf was revealed. For these emotional people this is an extremely difficult law. Once they were provoked, they were ready to do the greatest deeds. For them this is extremely burdensome, so burdensome that Hadrat Sa'd ibn Ubadah asks the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whether this law was indeed revealed in this manner. He asks questions, yet he knows that the law has indeed been revealed. Through this question he expresses the difficulty he feels, of how he would bear it if such a situation arose in his own house. He expresses this bitter reality by saying: "O Messenger of Allah, I know that this is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am astonished that if I saw a man placing his thigh upon the thigh of my wife, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him from his place until I brought four witnesses. By Allah, by the time I bring four witnesses he will have completed his task."

This was Sa'd ibn Ubadah's intellectual notion and thought. But a particular person, with his own ears and eyes, sees that this immorality is being done with his wife, and he holds back, and indeed the Qur'an has restrained him. This man controls his feelings, his thirst for revenge, his fierce Arab jealousy, the sudden surge of blood and the uncontrollable movement of his nerves. He exercises an unbreakable self-control which one cannot even imagine in Arab society. He comes helplessly and awaits the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Although this matter is extremely burdensome for him, the Qur'an had so trained these people that this man fully controls this storm of emotion, so that the command that is obeyed is the one that comes from Allah, both in his soul and in all the affairs of his person.

How was this training possible? It happened because they had complete certainty that Allah was with them, and that they were under Allah's watch and protection. Allah takes care of them and does not place them in a calamity they cannot bear, and does not leave them in difficulties that are unbearable for them. Allah never wrongs human beings. These people always lived under Allah's shade. They were breathing in an atmosphere of Allah's mercy and kindness. They were constantly looking towards Allah in the way a child looks towards his merciful and generous father. Hilal ibn Umayyah saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears. He was alone. He complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found no provision in the law except the enforcement of the hadd of qadhf. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) even announced that it was either testimony or the hadd on his back, but Hilal ibn Umayyah had the certainty that Allah would not leave him unsupported in such circumstances, since he was indeed truthful. Thus this exception came from Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave Hilal ibn Umayyah the good news, and he repeated his assurance, saying: "I had this hope from my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic." These people had complete assurance that they were under Allah's supervision, that Allah was watching, and that they had not been left to themselves to settle matters on their own. They were before Allah, in His court. This is true faith, obedience and submission and contentment, which was the distinguishing quality of the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Now the context moves beyond the middle of the law of hadd al-qadhf, and another glimpse of the vileness of the crime of qadhf is shown. Its connection is with the household of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The honour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself is at stake in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the most honoured servant of Allah. Then in this incident the honour of Hadrat Siddiq (رضي الله عنه) is also at stake, who is the most honoured person among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). Then there is also the matter of the honour of another Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal (رضي الله عنه). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself testifies that he knew nothing of Safwan except good. This incident is one in which the Muslims of Madinah remained in extreme distress for a month.

This is the account of the incident of al-ifk (the slander). This event subjected the purest people in human history to an extremely painful and distressing situation, and indeed put the entire Muslim community through the severest of trials. For a full month, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his most beloved wife Hadrat Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and her father Hadrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), a sincere believer, were kept in suspense. These pure hearts remained in anguish for a month.

It is appropriate that we hear this whole story from Hadrat Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) herself. Hadrat Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrates from her as follows:

"It was the custom of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that whenever he set out on a journey, he would draw lots to decide which of his wives would accompany him. On the occasion of the Ghazwah of Banu al-Mustaliq, the lot fell in my name, and I went with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. On the return journey, when we were close to Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ halted at a station during the night. While there was still part of the night left, preparations for departure began. I got up and went to relieve myself, and when I was returning toward the camp, I realised that my necklace had broken and fallen somewhere. I began searching for it, and in the meantime the caravan set off. The practice was that at the time of departure I would sit in my howdah (litter), and four men would lift it and place it on the camel. We women were very light at that time because of the scarcity of food. Therefore, while lifting the howdah, the people did not sense that I was not in it. They lifted the empty howdah, placed it on the camel and set off without knowing. When I returned with the necklace, there was no one there. I then wrapped myself in my veil and lay down in that very place, thinking that when they would not find me on reaching the next stop, they would come back searching for me. In that state, sleep overtook me. In the morning, Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami passed by the place where I was sleeping. He recognised me immediately, for he had seen me many times before the command of hijab had come down. (He was one of the Companions who fought at Badr, and he had the habit of sleeping late in the morning, so he too had been left behind at the camp site and was traveling to Madinah after waking up.) On seeing me, he stopped his camel, and involuntarily there came from his tongue: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' (Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we shall return). The wife of the Messenger of Allah had been left behind here! The sound of his voice woke me up. I quickly drew my veil over my face. He said nothing to me. He brought his camel and made it kneel before me and stood aside. I mounted the camel, and he led it by the rope and set off. Near midday we caught up with the army, which had just stopped at its place, and the people of the army did not yet know that I had been left behind. Then those who spread slander spread their slander, and at the forefront of them was Abdullah ibn Ubayy. But I was unaware of what they were saying about me. When I reached Madinah, I fell ill and remained on my bed for nearly a month. The rumours of the slander were spreading in the city, and they had reached the ears of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I knew nothing of it. What troubled me, however, was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not show me the attention that he used to show during my illness. When he came into the house, he would only ask those in the household, 'How is she?' (kayfa tikum, 'How are you?'), and would not speak to me directly. This caused me to suspect that something was indeed wrong. Finally, I obtained his permission and went to my mother's house, so that she could nurse me properly.

One night I went out of Madinah to relieve myself. At that time, our houses did not have lavatories, and we used to go out to the jungle. With me was Mistah ibn Uthathah's mother, who was a cousin of my father's mother. On the way she stumbled, and involuntarily there came from her tongue: 'May Mistah be destroyed!' I said: 'What a mother you are, cursing your son, and he is one who took part in Badr!' She said: 'O daughter, do you not know what he says?' Then she related the whole account to me, of what the slanderers were spreading about me. I went home and spent the night weeping. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Hadrat Ali and Usamah ibn Zayd after me, and asked them for their counsel. Usamah spoke a good word on my behalf and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have seen nothing in your wife but good. All of this being spread is falsehood and fabrication.' As for Hadrat Ali, he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, women are not in short supply. You may take another wife in her place, and if you wish to investigate, call the servant girl and question her about the situation.' So the servant girl was called and questioned. She said: 'By the God who sent you with the truth, I have never seen in her anything blameworthy on which a fault could be placed. The only fault is that I knead dough and tell her, "Mistress, keep an eye on the dough," but she falls asleep, and a goat comes and eats the dough.'

On that same day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon: 'O Muslims! Who will save my honour from the attacks of this man who has crossed the limit by accusing my family and causing me distress? By Allah, I have seen nothing in my wife but good, nor in the man about whom this accusation is being made. He never entered my house in my absence.' Then Usayd ibn Hudayr (in some narrations, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh) stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if he is from our tribe (Aws), we will cut off his head; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, then also give the command, and we are ready to carry it out.' On hearing this, Sa'd ibn Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj, stood up and said: 'You lie! You will never be able to kill him. You mention killing him only because he is from the Khazraj. If he had been from your tribe, you would never have said, "We will cut off his head."' Usayd ibn Hudayr replied: 'You are a hypocrite, and so you defend the hypocrites.' Then there was an uproar in the Prophet's Mosque, although the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was seated on the pulpit. It was close to the Aws and Khazraj fighting within the mosque itself, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ calmed them and then descended from the pulpit.

For nearly a month the rumours of this slander kept circulating in the city. The Prophet ﷺ was in severe distress. I kept weeping. My parents were extremely worried and grief-stricken. Finally, one day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and sat beside me; in all that period he had never sat beside me. Hadrat Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman sensed that some decisive matter was about to be settled, so both of them came and sat with me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Aishah, I have received this news about you. If you are innocent, Allah will surely make your innocence clear; and if you have indeed fallen into sin, then repent to Allah and seek forgiveness. When a servant acknowledges his sin and repents, Allah forgives.' On hearing these words, my tears dried up. I said to my father: 'Please answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on my behalf.' He said: 'Daughter, I do not understand what I should say.' I said to my mother: 'You say something.' She also said: 'I am at a loss as to what to say.' Then I said: 'A matter has entered your ears and settled in your hearts. Now if I say that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me. And if I confess to something I did not do, and Allah knows that I did not do it, you will accept it.' At that moment I tried to recall the name of Hadrat Ya'qub, but I could not remember it. Finally I said: 'In this situation, there is no course open to me except to say what the father of Hadrat Yusuf said: "So patience is most fitting" (fa-sabrun jamil).' Saying this, I lay down and turned to the other side. At that time I was saying to myself that Allah knows of my innocence and will surely reveal the truth. Yet it had not even crossed my mind or imagination that revelation would descend concerning me, which would be recited until the Day of Resurrection. I considered my own self too insignificant for Allah to speak on my behalf; rather I thought that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might see a dream in which Allah would make my innocence clear. Meanwhile, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was overtaken by that state which used to come upon him when revelation was descending, so that in the severe cold of winter, drops of sweat fell from his face like pearls. We all fell silent. I was completely fearless, but my parents were so terrified that it seemed as if not a drop of blood remained in their bodies. They were afraid to see what truth Allah would reveal. When that state passed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was extremely joyful. The first thing he said, smiling, was: 'Good news, Aishah! Allah has revealed your innocence.' After that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ten verses. My mother said: 'Get up and thank the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' I said: 'I will thank neither him nor you both, but I thank Allah, who revealed my innocence. You did not even deny the slander.'"

When these verses were revealed, Hadrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq swore that he would never again spend anything on Mistah. He was a poor man and a relative of Hadrat Siddiq, and Abu Bakr used to support him. Mistah too had taken part in the accusation against Hadrat Aishah. After this, the following verse was revealed:

﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear against giving to their relatives, the needy and those who emigrated in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not wish that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (24:22)

Hadrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "Yes, I wish and I love that Allah should forgive me." He then resumed the allowance he used to give Mistah, and said: "I will never stop this assistance." Hadrat Aishah says that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about me. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Zaynab, what do you know, and what have you seen?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I protect my eyes and ears. By Allah, I know nothing of her but good." She was the one who was my rival among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah saved her because of her God-fearing nature, but her sister Hamnah bint Jahsh fought on her behalf, and so she was destroyed along with those who were destroyed in the affair of the slander.

You have seen how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spent those days, and how Hadrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his family spent them. Consider also what befell poor Hadrat Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, and how all the Muslims passed those days, as though their breath was being choked, and every person was in severe affliction. These were the circumstances in which these verses were revealed. Before such distressing conditions, a person stands helpless. It was a painful event for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He saw that these circumstances were like a biting ordeal for his noble wife, who was very young. Her age was about sixteen. It is a most sensitive age, and a period of very deep love between spouses.

This young girl is innocent. Her conscience is clear and her thoughts are pure, yet this accusation is being levelled at her in the most delicate and sensitive matter. Her honour is at stake. She is the daughter of Siddiq, who lives in a most pure and exalted station. Her trustworthiness is being challenged. She is the wife of Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the chief of the Banu Hashim, and her loyalty is being made doubtful. She is the most beloved wife of a great Prophet, and there is a danger not only to the bond of that love being broken but also to her faith. She was raised at the very centre of faith; from the time she opened her eyes she saw nothing but faith, and then she became the wife of the last Prophet ﷺ.

She has been accused, and what a great accusation it is, from which she is entirely free and of which she is unaware. She does not understand what to do or what evidence to bring to show that she is chaste. She has only hope in Allah. She hopes that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will see in a dream the truth, that she is completely free of this accusation. But the dream does not come, and revelation has ceased. There was wisdom of Allah in this as well. A full month has passed, and this poor girl is sinking in that great torment.

Her condition becomes critical when she hears the full account from Umm Mistah. She is ill and her life is in danger, and in great anguish she says to her mother, "Glory be to Allah! Are people really saying these things?" In another narration, she asks in great distress whether her father has also come to know of it. Her mother says yes. She then asks whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has also come to know of it, and her mother says yes.

Then comes the moment when the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), the one she believed in and her husband, whom she loved intensely, addresses her directly. He says: "To proceed. Such and such things have reached me about you. If you are chaste, Allah will soon declare your innocence. And if you have committed a sin, then repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness, for when a servant acknowledges his sin and then repents, Allah forgives him."

From these words she clearly understands that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is also in doubt about her. He is not certain of her innocence. He has not given a decision regarding the accusation that has been made. Revelation from the Lord of Honour has also stopped. Allah has not sent down any declaration of her innocence, though she is certain that she is innocent. But what proof can this poor woman present? Night and day pass in this way, and even in that great heart she stands accused, although the Prophet (ﷺ) has a deep, wholehearted love for her.

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) is the loyal companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), extremely sensitive and pure of soul. He is in such a state that this grief is constantly gnawing at him. The honour of his family has been attacked, his beloved daughter, and she is also the wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It must be remembered that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the companion in whom he has complete certainty and confidence. Beyond being a friend, he is also his Prophet, in whom he believes. He confirms every word of the Prophet (ﷺ). He does not seek any external evidence about him at all. The pain in his heart is evident from his words, but he remains patient. He overcomes his pain and keeps himself under control. He says: "By Allah, even in the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah), this accusation was never levelled against us. Would we accept it now, in Islam?" This is a statement with great bitterness hidden within it. Even so, his daughter, who is also ill, is caught in severe torment. She pleads that he should answer the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Siddiq says: "By Allah, what can I say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this?"

Umm Ruman, the wife of the Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), consoles her wounded daughter in every way. Her sick daughter weeps so much that it seems her heart might burst. She says: "Daughter, have some mercy on yourself. By Allah, whenever a beautiful woman has been beloved to a man and has co-wives, they have levelled all kinds of accusations against her." But her consolations collapse at that moment. Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) says to her mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my behalf." Her mother also says the same thing her husband had said: "By Allah, I cannot say anything before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

And that Muslim, pious and striver in the way of Allah (mujahid fi sabilillah), is also in a strange position. Has a charge been levelled against him regarding the wife of his Prophet? In Islam, this grave accusation! His trustworthiness and integrity, his dignity and his zeal are at stake. In fact, his faith itself is in danger. When he hears of this accusation, he spontaneously says: "By Allah, I have never even uncovered the shoulder of any woman!" She is free even from the thought of that sin. Then he hears that Hassan ibn Thabit is saying disparaging words about her. He wants to strike off Hassan's head with a single blow of the sword, but he holds back, because he is a Muslim and a believer, and it is forbidden for a believer to raise a sword against another believer. What he is going through is more than he can bear; he is on the verge of losing control.

Then there is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is the Messenger of Allah and the pride of Banu Hashim. His household has been attacked, and within his household, Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) has been targeted. This is an attack on his home and on his most beloved wife. No proud Arab could bear this. A month has passed. The people of Madinah are whispering about it. But he is enduring it, and Allah, too, is watching everything, yet the wisdom of His plan required that a month pass. Muhammad (ﷺ) is also a human being. He feels pain and grief as a human being does. His heart is also wounded. He too feels distress, because the light of Allah, which always illuminates his heart in every matter and clears the path for him, is delayed. Although there were indications of his wife's innocence, the human heart is nonetheless a place where doubt can settle. Complete satisfaction is not achieved through indications alone, while the entire city of Madinah is burning in this fire. Doubt also passes through the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning his beloved wife, and he cannot entirely remove it from his heart. After all, he is a human being and a mortal. Like other people, he too is affected. He is a husband, yet he cannot go to his wife. When the seed of doubt is sown in a person's heart and settles there permanently, that doubt can only be removed by a decisive proof and a conclusive event.

This burden takes hold of the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). He summons his beloved Usamah ibn Zayd, who was very dear to him and close to his heart, and he also summons his son-in-law and paternal cousin, Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and consults with them. As for Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), he is among the asbah (agnatic kinsmen) of the Messenger (ﷺ). For this reason also, his feelings are very intense. Moreover, the distress, sorrow and suffering that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is enduring also weighs heavily upon Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), because he is a paternal cousin. He advises that Allah has not placed any hardship upon the Prophet (ﷺ). Yet, for the sake of the Prophet's peace of mind, he also says that he should question the servant girl about Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), for she is a serving girl.

As for Usamah, he knows how deep the love of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is for his wife, and that he has been separated from his spouse for a long time. So he says plainly that the Mother of the Believers is pure and chaste, and that those who make these accusations are liars.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) draws strength from the statements and testimony of Usamah and the servant girl, amid this human anxiety and this human distress. He gathers the people in the mosque and places the matter before them. On that occasion he said: "Who will deal with those people who have attacked the honour of my family? They have levelled an accusation against his wife, and have accused a virtuous and respectable man among the Muslims, a man about whom they know nothing bad." At that gathering, a dispute arose between Aws and Khazraj (the two tribes of the Ansar), even though they were in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself was present. This shows what terrifying shadows were hovering over the Muslims at that strange time, and what the atmosphere of Madinah was like. The sanctity of leadership itself was at stake. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also felt a sting in his heart, and the light (revelation) that had always guided him in such circumstances was also withheld. In such circumstances the Prophet (ﷺ) goes to Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), asks her what the people are saying, and takes a full and detailed account from her.

When these afflictions reach their peak, Allah, the Exalted, has mercy upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and upon the Muslims. The Qur'an is revealed, and the innocence of Aishah the Siddiqah (may Allah be pleased with her) is declared. The Word of Allah comes in defence of the household of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the hypocrites who had played the most active part in this trial are exposed. Then permanent guidance is given to the Islamic society in such circumstances, and legislation and a code of moral conduct are established.

Concerning these verses of the Holy Qur'an, Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I knew that I was innocent, and I was certain that Allah would bear witness to my innocence. But it never occurred to me that the Qur'an would be revealed about me and my innocence, and that it would be recited until the Day of Resurrection. In my view, I was not worthy that Allah would speak about me and that His speech would be recited. However, I did know, and I hoped, that perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream in which my innocence would be established."

This detailed account makes it clear that this matter was not merely about Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) personally. It also concerned the Prophet (ﷺ) himself. This incident enveloped the leadership of the Muslim ummah, and its impact was falling upon the relationship between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Allah Himself. This was not merely an accusation against Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her); it was an accusation against the Islamic worldview, against the Prophet of Islam and the founder of Islam. This is why Allah, in this matter, sent down His own decision, so that the threads and fabric of this conspiracy would be scattered, and so that the conspiracy which the hypocrites had devised against Islam and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be brought to an end. And whatever secret and wisdom lay behind it, Allah would reveal it, since knowledge of it belonged to Allah alone.

(Indeed, those who came up with the slander...) (24:11): ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you. Do not consider it a bad thing for you; rather, it is good for you. For every man among them is what he has earned of sin, and he who took upon himself the greater part of it will have a great punishment.﴾

They were not a few individuals but a faction. These people were mixed in among you, and all of them had one single aim. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was not the only person who spread this lie, though he was responsible for the greater part of it. This group was made up of Jews and hypocrites. They had been defeated by Islam on the battlefield, and now, working behind the scenes, they plotted against Islam. The incident of the slander (ifk) was one of their conspiracies. Some believers also became involved in this affair, such as Hamnah bint Jahsh, Hassan ibn Thabit, and Mistah ibn Uthathah. But the real conspiracy was devised by this group, and the ringleader of this group was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He was so cunning that he did not appear openly in this campaign. Outwardly he said nothing that could be used to seize him and enforce the prescribed punishment (hadd) against him. He would whisper with those who were trusted by him and who were not prepared to give evidence against him. He carried on this campaign with such skill that the whole of Madinah burned for a month in an atmosphere like a volcano and an earthquake. People talked about the purest household in this world. Here, the verses begin by speaking of this central subject at the very outset, so that its importance becomes clear, and so that people know that behind it there is a group which was devising such a deep conspiracy against Islam. This was a great assault against Islam, the believers, and the person of the Prophet (ﷺ).

After this, the believers are quickly reassured:

﴿Do not consider it a bad thing for you; rather, it is good for you.﴾ (24:11) This is good for you, because those who devised the conspiracy of the slander were, in truth, enemies of Islam, taking aim at the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and at his household. From this incident, the need for the hadd al-qadhf (the prescribed punishment for slander) is also established from the Islamic point of view. It also shows how many tongues would be raised against chaste women, and what dangers would arise for the Islamic community and the new Islamic society, if tongues were left unrestrained. Such accusations could even reach the Prophet's household and destroy noble families, and as a result modesty, shame, caution, purity and respect for human dignity could vanish from society.

Furthermore, this taught the Islamic society how to deal with such emotionally provocative matters, and how never to lose dignity and seriousness even in emotional affairs.

As for the pains and sufferings which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his household, and all the believers endured, these are the price of the experience gained through such trials. In a trial, such sacrifices must be made, and in the fulfilment of duties such stages also come.

Those who were active in this affair of slander each received a share of it in proportion to their crime.
