This scene is presented very calmly and at length. One is invited to reflect on every part of this scene. The parts of this scene are gathered again. The meaning is that through deep observation and contemplation, the human sense is awakened, and the human feeling is sharpened regarding the profound craftsmanship and the deep insight within it, so that a person may see this scene with eyes that take heed.

God drives the clouds from one region to another. These clouds appear in the sky in scattered pieces. Then they gather together. Suddenly we see layers forming upon layers. When they become sufficiently heavy, water begins to pour out of them. You see large, heavy drops of rain falling. These clouds appear in the heavens like great mountains. When they rise very high, ice forms within them. These clouds look very much like mountains. When an aircraft rises above them, these clouds in fact appear as mountains: great mountains, with great highs and lows within them. This manner of expression is such that a person only fully understood it when he rode in an aircraft and rose above the clouds.

These mountains of clouds are bound by God's command and God's system. They work in accordance with His cosmic order. God gives water through them to whomever He wills, and He turns them away from whomever He wills. The completion of this scene comes thus:

﴿يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْأَبْصَارِ﴾ (24:43) "The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight." This scene has been brought so that the light of lightning becomes one with the Great Light of the universe. It is the particular style of the Holy Qur'an to bring together meanings of the same kind in one place, because this surah is Surah an-Nur.

Now the third cosmic scene, the scene of the alternation of night and day, lies before us:

﴿يُقَلِّبُ اللَّهُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ﴾ "God alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have sight."

Reflection upon the system of the alternation of night and day is an important theme of the Holy Qur'an. This system of the changing of night and day continues without interruption, and there is not a moment's change or alteration within it. Through it, that order which governs this universe becomes well known. Through reflection upon this order, it becomes clearly known with what precision God runs this system. The Qur'an, with its effective style of expression, renews the impressions of these scenes which, through being familiar, have generally faded away. A person then sees these scenes with a new sense and takes a completely new impression each time. Think of it this way: if a person were to see this system of the alternation of night and day for the first time, what would his impression be? Even after centuries have passed, no change has occurred in this system. If there is any change, it is only in the human gaze. The human sense and perception have grown dim in viewing the scenes of the alternation of night and day, whereas this system of night and day has not lessened anything of its beauty and wonder. When a person passes over this universe heedlessly, like the unaware, he loses a great joy of life; indeed, the true beauty of this universe vanishes from his sight. Those scenes, if presented again before a person, would be very impactful and appear beautiful.

The marvel of the Qur'an is that it revives our dulled sense and renews our hidden consciousness and sleeping feelings. Our cold heart becomes warm and our intuition becomes sharp. Then we begin to see this universe as though we had seen it for the first time. We again reflect upon the phenomena of this universe and begin to discover its hidden and concealed perfections. Then we see that the hand of divine power is working everywhere. In everything around us there is His craftsmanship, in everything in this universe there are His signs, and for us there are lessons upon lessons.

God continually bestows His favour upon us: whenever we reflect upon any scene of this universe, we receive a fresh life. We gain a new feeling about everything in this universe, and thus we find joy as though we were seeing this scene for the first time. In this feeling, we discover this universe many times over and countless times, and we find delight. If viewed with perceptive eyes, this universe is very beautiful, and our nature is in harmony with the nature of the universe. Our nature springs from the same fountainhead from which this universe has derived its existence, its nature, and the order of its nature. When we become joined with the spirit of this universe, we find a strange tranquillity and peace, a very deep connection and joy. We find intimacy and serenity, just as a person meets his beloved directly.

As a result of deep recognition of this universe, we see in it the light of God, and this is the meaning of God's light of the heavens and the earth. When we deeply observe our own existence, our own self, and this universe, we see in it the light of God, and at that time we have reached the real truth, and we see what the reality of the governance of the universe is.

This is why the Qur'an repeatedly draws our attention to observe the everyday scenes of this universe with deeper reflection. For our perception and our contemplation, the Qur'an repeatedly presents diverse scenes and phenomena which are extremely beautiful. The Qur'an calls us not to pass over these phenomena and scenes heedlessly, eyes closed, because this journey of yours in this world is extremely purposeful. Take something from here when you go, but humans are going away empty-handed.

Further evidences of divine power are presented, and our sense is sharpened even more, so that we realise that on one single principle this life is established here. It has one single temperament. After one such creation, there are again many observations and manifestations of life, and in it there is variety.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 45:

(Wallahu khalaqa ... qadir) (45)

This is a great truth, which the Noble Qur'an expresses in extremely simple words. The fact that every living creature has been created from water shows that the fundamental elements of life are one and the same, and that the fundamental element for the sustenance of life is water. Modern science too is moving toward the view that the original creation of life took place in water, that is, in the sea. In other words, in its initial state life was in water. After that, diversity came into being within life. This is the thinking of the scientists.

Our thinking is different. We do not impose Qur'anic truths upon the standards of science, because the principles and criteria of science change, whereas the Qur'an presents unchanging and final truths. We simply say that the origin of life is water, because the Qur'an says so. Although the forms of life appear different, its essential substance is indeed water. It is from water that living beings began to walk upon the earth.

Yakhluqu Allahu ma yasha'u (24:45): "Allah creates whatever He wills." He creates animals of different structures and different forms, and it is the will of Allah that determines what He creates and in what form He creates it.

Inna Allaha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (24:45): "Indeed, Allah is over all things competent." If we reflect upon all living things, we will see that the origin of life is one, yet from this one substance Allah has made what kinds of things and in what forms. Of different sizes, of different colours, of different shapes and appearances. Thus it becomes evident that there is one Creator and Administrator who produces this diversity, and who has power over all things.

From this deep study it also becomes known that nothing in this universe has come into being merely by chance and without will, but rather it has come about through planning and purpose. If the planning and will of the Creator is not accepted, then what chance is it that brought it into being? Moreover, it is a strange coincidence that a planning and a destiny arose within each thing on its own.

The reality is that this entire universe is the craftsmanship of Allah, who granted every thing its creation and granted every thing guidance, instinct and consciousness of what its duty is.

Lesson No. 155: At a Glance

The previous great section and the long lesson were on the subject of Light, and this Light was also among the manifestations of this universe. Now the discourse returns once more to its principal theme, namely the etiquette upon which the Qur'an wishes to build the Islamic society, and in accordance with which it is desired to purify the outward and inward lives of Muslims. It is also desired to illuminate the Islamic society with the same light by which this entire universe is illuminated (that is, the Islamic system too is a light, since the one who sent it down is also a light).

Regarding what kind of people are illuminated by the light of Allah: in the previous lesson a glimpse of them was shown, that they are people whom trade and buying and selling do not distract from the remembrance of Allah, and who, because of worldly affairs, do not neglect the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat. And of those who were deprived of this light of the universe, a glimpse was also shown there, that the worldly aims behind which they run night and day are a mirage, and that there is nothing in reality. Their life is like a boat enveloped in waves, above which are dense clouds, and nothing is visible.

Now here is mention of those hypocrites who are not ready to take any lesson from the clear signs of Allah. They display Islam, but they do not adopt the etiquette of the believers. The believers are those who are always ready to obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and who obey with the utmost tranquillity, seriousness and willing acceptance. Here a comparison is drawn between their faith and the faith of the truthful believers. Allah has promised the people of faith that they will be given the caliphate of the earth, and their authority will be firmly established upon this earth. This reward will be given to them because they maintain a relationship of the utmost respect and obedience with Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they honour Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Their this relationship with Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ exists despite the reality that the disbelievers are enemies of Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that the people of disbelief cannot render Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ powerless on this globe. The disbelievers' own end is destined to be evil.

Lesson No. 155: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 46 to 57

(Laqad anzalna... mustaqim) (46)

The words of Allah are a clear statement of reality. From them the light of Allah is known. They point to the pure springs of guidance. In these verses it is shown what good is and what evil is, what is pure and what is impure. These verses explain the Islamic system of life in a very detailed manner. These verses clearly reveal the laws and regulations to be implemented on earth, so that whenever people wish to make their decisions, the commands and laws are clear. In these laws there is no violation of the rights of any party. Nor is there any confusion between truth and falsehood. Nor is there any confusion between the lawful and the unlawful. Everything is clear and detailed.

(Wallahu... mustaqim) (24:46) "And Allah guides whom He wills to the straight path." Allah's will is unrestricted and is not bound by any condition. Yes, Allah has established a principle for guidance: whoever turns his self towards this path of guidance finds the way of guidance, but whoever turns away and does not seek the path in the light which Allah has scattered in this universe, goes along the way of misguidance. This misguidance also occurs in accordance with Allah's will.

In the following verses there is mention of a group that was very active in Madinah. This group was the hypocrites, who outwardly were Muslims and lived according to Islamic ways, but inwardly were darker still.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verses 47–50:

(ویقولون۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ بالمئو منین واذا۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ معرضون وان۔۔۔۔۔۔ مذعنین افی ۔۔۔۔۔۔ اولئک ھم الظلمون ) (5047) ” ۔ “۔

When correct faith settles in the heart, its effects appear in the form of action. Islam is a dynamic ideology and has no negative aspect. It is an ideology such that when it settles in the consciousness of a person, it begins to move on its own and its effects start to become visible outwardly. Islam itself begins to interpret itself through Islamic deeds. The method of the Islamic system of life is also this: it is a practical system, and it comes into being through action and movement. That is, Islam is a consciousness which manifests itself through action and conduct. Then, by becoming a permanent constitution and law in practice, it takes the form of a civilization. Its life depends on its primary consciousness. It is necessary to keep this consciousness and faith alive and moving.

But what kind of people are those being spoken of here? They used to say:

﴿We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey﴾ (24:47). "These people say that we have believed in Allah and the Messenger ﷺ, and we have accepted obedience." They used to say this with their mouths, but no trace of it appeared in their conduct. Thus they would turn back on their heels; their deeds would belie what they said with their tongues.

﴿And those are not believers﴾ (24:47). "Such people are certainly not believers." Believers are those whose deeds confirm their words. Faith is not a game, such that a person merely professes faith and thereafter has no responsibility. After faith, his self too should be dyed in the colours of faith. His heart, mind and thought should also become faithful. And after that, it is necessary that this person's actions too be faithful; and when faith settles in someone's conscience, then it becomes impossible for him to turn back from the path of faith.

These people claimed faith, but in practice they were opposed to the meaning and implication of faith. When they were told, "Come, let your dispute be decided according to the law of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and according to the Shariah revealed upon Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ," they turned away.

﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away﴾ (24:48–49). "When these people are called to Allah and His Messenger, so that the Messenger may judge between them, a faction of them shies away. However, if the truth is in their favour, they come to the Messenger ﷺ as very obedient people." Because they knew that the command of Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not far from truth, and that the Messenger ﷺ had no room for personal desires in his judgments, and that even if there were enmity, the Messenger of Allah would decide according to truth. Therefore, these people, when they knew that their position was against the truth, would flee from the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and refuse to come before him; and if they were in the right, they would run to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as very pleased and cheerful people, happily, because they were certain that the Prophet ﷺ does not deviate from the truth, and that in the court of the Shariah no one's right is lost.

These people, who claimed faith and yet adopted this duplicity, are a supreme example and standard for recognising the people of hypocrisy in every age. These people do not have the courage to openly announce their disbelief. Outwardly they are Muslims, but they do not like an Islamic colour to arise within society and a judicial system to be established according to Islamic laws. When such people are invited to come for judgment according to the Shariah, they turn away from it and put forward excuses.

﴿And those are not believers﴾ (24:47). "These people are not believers." Because faith and refusal to judge by the Islamic Shariah cannot come together in one place, unless judgment by the Islamic Shariah is in the interest of these hypocrites, in which case they come running.

Living according to the decisions of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is a sign of faith. This is the sign by which it can be known that the reality of faith has settled in the hearts, and for Muslims it is necessary to adopt this attitude in relation to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. Only a person who is extremely insolent and disobedient can reject the command of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, one who has not received any Islamic upbringing and whose heart is not illuminated by the light of faith.

This is why, as a result of their act, such questions are asked which reveal the sickness of their hearts. In these questions, astonishment is expressed as to why they are in doubt and why their conduct is wrong and deserving of hatred.

﴿Is there a disease in their hearts? Or are they in doubt? Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them?﴾ (24:50). The first question is for affirmation, meaning that in reality these people are hypocrites, and this is the effect of hypocrisy. No sound-natured person can practise this hypocrisy, because these are natural obligations and their nature is no longer healthy. In reality, they have not seen the reality of faith, and these people are proceeding on the highway of ambiguity.

The second question is for astonishment. The wonder is that, while claiming faith, they still have doubt about the decisions of Allah. Is it that they doubt that these commands come from Allah? Or they doubt whether Islam can establish a system of justice or not. Both of these matters are contrary to the ways of the believers.

The third question is for both the expression of hatred and the expression of astonishment. The astonishment and hatred are at the fact that these people doubt that perhaps Allah and His Messenger ﷺ will wrong them. It is a strange thing that a human being should doubt this, or fear that Allah would not act justly. Is it not Allah who is the Creator and Lord of all? Therefore how could He make distinctions among His creatures?

The command of Allah is one; there is not even a trace of oppression or injustice in it, because Allah is the Just One who does not wrong anyone in any way. All His creation is equal before Him; therefore He does not wrong one servant for the sake of the interest of another servant. Regarding the commands of all other individuals and institutions apart from Allah, it is possible to doubt that they may be oppressive, because if a human being is legislating for himself, one may suspect that the legislating human will look after his own interests. Whether the legislator is an individual or an institution, this suspicion may arise.

When a single person is the ruler, it is clear that he will legislate in his own favour and for his own interest. Likewise, if one government legislates for others, or one class legislates for others, or one bloc legislates for other blocs, the legislator may take his own interests into account. But when Allah legislates, there is no consideration of support for any individual, any group, any class, or any bloc. It is absolute justice, and this characteristic, that is, unrestricted justice, is possible only in the legislation of Allah. No judgment other than the judgment of Allah possesses this characteristic.

This is why those who are not content with the command of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ are themselves the wrongdoers. These people do not want absolute justice to take root on earth. These people do not want the authority of truth. These people, in this matter, are not afraid to doubt that there would be some oppression in the command of Allah; or rather, they have doubt in the justice of Allah.

﴿Nay, but they are the wrongdoers﴾ (24:50). "Rather, these people are in reality wrongdoers," because they do not want justice.

As for those who are truly Muslims, their attitude regarding Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is entirely different. When they are called to come and have judgments made according to the command of Allah and His Messenger, they say something entirely different. This statement is worthy of believers, and this statement shows that their hearts are illuminated with faith and are shining.

Its life depends on its primary consciousness. It is necessary to keep this consciousness and faith alive and moving.

But what kind of people are those being spoken of here? They used to say:

﴿We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey﴾ (24:47). "These people say that we have believed in Allah and the Messenger ﷺ, and we have accepted obedience." They used to say this with their mouths, but no trace of it appeared in their conduct. Thus they would turn back on their heels; their deeds would belie what they said with their tongues.

﴿And those are not believers﴾ (24:47). "Such people are certainly not believers." Believers are those whose deeds confirm their words. Faith is not a game, such that a person merely professes faith and thereafter has no responsibility. After faith, his self too should be dyed in the colours of faith. His heart, mind and thought should also become faithful. And after that, it is necessary that this person's actions too be faithful; and when faith settles in someone's conscience, then it becomes impossible for him to turn back from the path of faith.

These people claimed faith, but in practice they were opposed to the meaning and implication of faith. When they were told, "Come, let your dispute be decided according to the law of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and according to the Shariah revealed upon Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ," they turned away.

﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away﴾ (24:48–49). "When these people are called to Allah and His Messenger, so that the Messenger may judge between them, a faction of them shies away. However, if the truth is in their favour, they come to the Messenger ﷺ as very obedient people." Because they knew that the command of Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not far from truth, and that the Messenger ﷺ had no room for personal desires in his judgments, and that even if there were enmity, the Messenger of Allah would decide according to truth. Therefore, these people, when they knew that their position was against the truth, would flee from the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and refuse to come before him; and if they were in the right, they would run to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as very pleased and cheerful people, happily, because they were certain that the Prophet ﷺ does not deviate from the truth, and that in the court of the Shariah no one's right is lost.

These people, who claimed faith and yet adopted this duplicity, are a supreme example and standard for recognising the people of hypocrisy in every age. These people do not have the courage to openly announce their disbelief. Outwardly they are Muslims, but they do not like an Islamic colour to arise within society and a judicial system to be established according to Islamic laws. When such people are invited to come for judgment according to the Shariah, they turn away from it and put forward excuses.

﴿And those are not believers﴾ (24:47). "These people are not believers." Because faith and refusal to judge by the Islamic Shariah cannot come together in one place, unless judgment by the Islamic Shariah is in the interest of these hypocrites, in which case they come running.

Living according to the decisions of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is a sign of faith. This is the sign by which it can be known that the reality of faith has settled in the hearts, and for Muslims it is necessary to adopt this attitude in relation to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. Only a person who is extremely insolent and disobedient can reject the command of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, one who has not received any Islamic upbringing and whose heart is not illuminated by the light of faith.

This is why, as a result of their act, such questions are asked which reveal the sickness of their hearts. In these questions, astonishment is expressed as to why they are in doubt and why their conduct is wrong and deserving of hatred.

﴿Is there a disease in their hearts? Or are they in doubt? Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them?﴾ (24:50). The first question is for affirmation, meaning that in reality these people are hypocrites, and this is the effect of hypocrisy. No sound-natured person can practise this hypocrisy, because these are natural obligations and their nature is no longer healthy. In reality, they have not seen the reality of faith, and these people are proceeding on the highway of ambiguity.

The second question is for astonishment. The wonder is that, while claiming faith, they still have doubt about the decisions of Allah. Is it that they doubt that these commands come from Allah? Or they doubt whether Islam can establish a system of justice or not. Both of these matters are contrary to the ways of the believers.

The third question is for both the expression of hatred and the expression of astonishment. The astonishment and hatred are at the fact that these people doubt that perhaps Allah and His Messenger ﷺ will wrong them. It is a strange thing that a human being should doubt this, or fear that Allah would not act justly. Is it not Allah who is the Creator and Lord of all? Therefore how could He make distinctions among His creatures?

The command of Allah is one; there is not even a trace of oppression or injustice in it, because Allah is the Just One who does not wrong anyone in any way. All His creation is equal before Him; therefore He does not wrong one servant for the sake of the interest of another servant. Regarding the commands of all other individuals and institutions apart from Allah, it is possible to doubt that they may be oppressive, because if a human being is legislating for himself, one may suspect that the legislating human will look after his own interests. Whether the legislator is an individual or an institution, this suspicion may arise.

When a single person is the ruler, it is clear that he will legislate in his own favour and for his own interest. Likewise, if one government legislates for others, or one class legislates for others, or one bloc legislates for other blocs, the legislator may take his own interests into account. But when Allah legislates, there is no consideration of support for any individual, any group, any class, or any bloc. It is absolute justice, and this characteristic, that is, unrestricted justice, is possible only in the legislation of Allah. No judgment other than the judgment of Allah possesses this characteristic.

This is why those who are not content with the command of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ are themselves the wrongdoers. These people do not want absolute justice to take root on earth. These people do not want the authority of truth. These people, in this matter, are not afraid to doubt that there would be some oppression in the command of Allah; or rather, they have doubt in the justice of Allah.

﴿Nay, but they are the wrongdoers﴾ (24:50). "Rather, these people are in reality wrongdoers," because they do not want justice.

As for those who are truly Muslims, their attitude regarding Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is entirely different. When they are called to come and have judgments made according to the command of Allah and His Messenger, they say something entirely different. This statement is worthy of believers, and this statement shows that their hearts are illuminated with faith and are shining.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 51:

(Innama kana...ulaika humul-muflihun) (51) "The attitude of these people is that they obey and submit without any questioning or the slightest deviation. They render this obedience and submission because they have complete confidence and firm conviction that the decision of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is the true decision, and that it is absolutely just and fair. Whatever lies beyond this is based on carnal desires. They render this obedience and submission because they have wholly bowed themselves before Allah. They believe that it is Allah who gives life, it is Allah who has control over this universe, and they are satisfied that what Allah wills for people is better than what people will for themselves, because the One who created them knows best about His creation.

Wa ulaika humul-muflihun (24:51) "Such people are the ones who attain success." They are successful because the Creator of the universe Himself manages their affairs and He Himself organizes their mutual relations. With His knowledge and justice, He makes the decisions among them. Therefore, they ought to be better than those people who decide their own affairs themselves, or those like them. These people, and their own fellow human beings, do not possess the knowledge and wisdom that Allah possesses. Furthermore, they will be successful because they are walking on one single path, in which there is no crookedness or deviation. They are content with this path. They are walking on this path. They do not wander here and there. Therefore their powers are not scattered, and there is no contradiction in their desires. They are not led by the reins of desires and interests; rather, their reins are in the hand of the Islamic path, which goes before them, and they follow behind it.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, Verses 52–53:**

(﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah and keeps his duty to Him (taqwa), it is those who are the attainers (of success).﴾) (52)

The subject of the previous verse was that the believers are obedient to the decisions of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). Here it is said that it is the practice of the believers to observe the commands and prohibitions of Allah beyond legal judgments. They do this obedience not out of fear of legal punishment, but out of fear of Allah's grip (punishment). *Taqwa* (God-consciousness, piety) is a more general word than *khashyah* (awe and fear), because khashyah carries the aspect of fear and dread, whereas taqwa, progressing further, creates in a person the awareness of caution in both small and great matters. The one who fears Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and obeys them is the one who attains success. Such a person attains salvation in this world and in the Hereafter. This is Allah's promise, and Allah does not go against His promise. Such people are certainly counted among those who attain success, and in their lives there are such means that become the cause of their success, because whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) is in fact walking on the straight path (*manhaj*, methodology) determined by Allah. This *manhaj* succeeds because Allah Himself has established it on the foundation of knowledge and wisdom. Within the nature and temperament of this *manhaj* lies this success, both the success of this world and that of the Hereafter. Then, in this system, the fear of Allah and taqwa are the guards that keep people on this system, and so the system remains upright. On the straight path on which they walk, deceptive things constantly cling to them everywhere, but these people do not deviate from their way.

These etiquettes, that a person obeys Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) with fear of God, taqwa and khashyah, are extremely elevated etiquettes of life. From them it becomes clear that the hearts of such people are illuminated with the divine light. These hearts are connected to Allah, and the awareness of the fear of Allah is settled in their consciousness. And from these etiquettes it becomes clear that these hearts are extremely honourable and exalted, because no noble person likes to be humiliated and disgraced before people like himself, and therefore the conscience of a believer recoils from this. Indeed, true obedience is that in which the one who obeys does so with the view that he is obeying the Majestic Being, because a true believer can bow his head only before Allah.

After this comparison between the good etiquettes of the believers and the bad etiquettes of the hypocrites, namely that the believers are those who bow only before Allah, while the hypocrites are those who claim faith but are not believers, now the discussion about the hypocrites is continued to its conclusion.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 24, verse 54:

(Wa aqsamu... ...illal-balagh al-mubin) (52:53)

The hypocrites would come before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and swear oaths that if you ordered them to fight, they would certainly go out. But Allah knows well that they are liars. Allah most contemptuously rejects this assurance of theirs.

﴿Say: "Do not swear. Known obedience is what is wanted"﴾ (24:53). That is, say to them: "Do not swear oaths; your obedience is already known." Everyone knows what kind of obedience you render, and there is no need now to take oaths on such obedience. This is said to a person whose lying is known and who is notorious as a liar. It is as if it is said: "Enough, do not swear; you are well known as truthful. Why is there any need for an oath?"

After this mocking tone, it is also said:

﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ (24:53). That is, Allah is aware of all your deeds. Therefore you have no need of oaths and emphatic assurances. Allah knows that if you are commanded, you will neither go out nor fight.

Then the command to obey is given again, in earnest. That is, it is said: render true obedience, not the kind of obedience that is known of you.

﴿Say: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger"﴾ (24:54). That is, say to them: be obedient to Allah and follow the Messenger's commands. ﴿But if you turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been charged﴾ (24:54). That is, if you turn your faces away, oppose the commands of Allah and His Messenger, and do not implement them, then the Messenger is responsible only for the duty placed upon him. His duty is to convey the message of prophethood, and he has discharged this duty in the best manner.

﴿And upon you is only that with which you have been charged﴾ (24:54). Your responsibility is to obey and to believe sincerely. You have turned away from this, and you have not fully discharged this responsibility.

﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾ (24:54). That is, you will come onto the right path and, living under a sound system, you will attain success in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ (24:54). The Messenger's responsibility is nothing more than to convey the command plainly. The Messenger (ﷺ) will not be asked whether you believed or not, and he will not be held guilty because of your turning away. You will be the guilty ones, and you alone will be punished for it. The charge against you will be that you violated the commands of Allah and of the Messenger of Allah.

After explaining the matter of the hypocrites, the discourse now sets them aside, and its direction turns toward the obedient believers. It is described what their reward will be in this world, and what the blessings and honours of the Hereafter will be.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 24, verse 55:

(Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds... they are the defiantly disobedient.) (55) ""

This is a promise to those members of the Muhammadan community who believe and do righteous deeds. The promise is that they will be granted supreme authority on this earth, and that the religion of Islam, which Allah has chosen for them, will be granted dominance. He will transform their state of fear into a state of peace and tranquility. This is the promise of Allah, and the promise of Allah is always true; the promise of Allah always comes to pass, and Allah never breaks His promise. The question is: what kind of believers are they to whom Allah has promised that authority on earth will be given to them?

The reality of that faith, which results in Allah's promise that the believers will be granted supreme authority on earth, is a great reality, and that reality encompasses the whole of human life. When this reality settles in a person's heart, it manifests and is declared in practical form. All of that person's activities turn towards Allah. This believing man begins working for the pleasure of Allah. He bows his head before Allah's obedience and His commands and laws, in both small and great matters. Then no desire of his self remains in any matter. There is no lust in his heart, and no crookedness remains in his nature, and this believer begins to obey Allah and the Messenger of Allah in all these matters.

This faith is such that a person becomes completely immersed in it. His thoughts are steeped in this faith; the beat of his heart is faith. The inclinations of his soul are in matters of faith. The inclinations of his nature, the movements of his body, the motions of his limbs, his conduct towards his Lord and his dealings with the common people are all dyed in the colour of Allah, and all these things are present in the verse of succession (istikhlaf). Allah Himself explains when this grant of supreme authority will occur.

"They shall worship Me and not associate anything with Me" (24:55). Shirk has many kinds. Turning towards anyone other than Allah in beliefs, in actions, or in consciousness is also shirk.

It becomes clear that faith is the name of a complete system of life. It includes all the commands of Allah. And when all these commands are practically established in human life, all the means of supreme authority are provided. Preparation is complete, resources are provided, and the person then becomes able to bear the great trust and supreme authority; that is, the trust of being Allah's vicegerent (khalifah) on earth is entrusted to him.

What is the meaning of istikhlaf fi al-ardh, or supreme authority over the earth? It does not mean merely that a people receive government, power and the authority to enforce orders. Rather, the meaning of being Allah's vicegerent is that they use those powers for reform, construction and development. Through them they pave the way for the system of life which Allah has sent for all humankind, so that all of humanity may walk on that path, and man may attain on this earth the perfection that Allah has destined for him, and by which man has been honoured.

Allah's vicegerent is not one who carries out corruption and destruction in the world, but one who takes part in the reform, construction and development of this world and gives justice and equity to the world. It must not be that he oppresses people and, instead of raising the standard of humanity, lowers it. He must not oppress instead of reforming the system that exists among people. He must not reduce good people to the level of animality, but rather raise those people who have fallen to the level of animals.

This is the supreme authority which Allah promises to the people of faith: that Allah keeps giving them such authority on earth so that they may fulfil Allah's purpose on this globe. And what is Allah's purpose? That they bring humanity to the perfection of humanity, a perfection which Allah had destined for it from the very day of creation. But those who come to power on earth and thereby spread corruption, establish rebellion and oppression on earth, and reduce humanity to the level of animality, these people are not caliphs from Allah on this earth; rather, they are followers of Satan. This position is given to them as a trial, and they are imposed upon people as a punishment.

The concept of this succession that we have understood is indicated within this very verse. It says:

"He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them" (24:55). And religion can be established only when it settles into the hearts of the believers. When it is firmly enforced in every action of their lives. When faith settles well in their lives and their hearts, they will attain istikhlaf fi al-ardh. The religion Allah has chosen for them will become dominant on earth, and what their religion commands includes reform, justice, and control over human desires. Moreover, benefiting from and seeking the bounties placed within the earth is also included in it, provided that in all these activities the direction and qibla of a person is Allah alone.

"And He will surely change their state of fear into security" (24:55). The Muslims in Mecca were in fear. The state of security was extremely doubtful. They remained armed at all times, and at no time were they permitted to keep weapons. Even after the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims migrated, they remained armed. Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Abu al-Aliyah regarding this verse that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions called to the worship of One God alone for more than ten years in Mecca, calling only to the worship of Allah alone, and forbidding every kind of shirk. They used to convey this call secretly, and they were always subject to fear. The believers were forbidden to fight. After the migration, when they were permitted to fight in Medina, they still mostly lived in a state of fear there. They remained armed morning and evening. They were patient with this kind of life for a long time. One of the companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we always remain in fear like this? Will there not come a time when we may put down our weapons and live in peace and security?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be patient a little longer; one of you will be in a great gathering and will not have even a small piece of iron with him." At that occasion Allah revealed this verse. When the Prophet ﷺ gained dominance over the Arabian Peninsula, they believed and laid down their arms. After that Allah took the Prophet ﷺ, and the Muslims lived in peace under the leadership of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman (may Allah be pleased with them). After that they became involved in those events in which they became involved, so Allah again afflicted them with fear, and they adopted guards and police and so on. They changed, so Allah also changed them.

"And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the defiantly disobedient" (24:55). These are people who abandon Allah's conditions and break the covenant and pledge made with Allah. Allah's promise was fulfilled once and remained in force as long as the Muslims continued to fulfil Allah's conditions, namely:

"They shall worship Me and not associate anything with Me" (24:55). Their carnal desires will not become their gods. They will not commit shirk, and they will remain steadfast in the worship of Allah. This promise of Allah still holds for every group of believers and will remain in force until the Day of Resurrection. At any time when a group of believers is not Allah's vicegerent, is not established on earth, and is not in peace, it is because it is not fulfilling the broader conditions of that promise and covenant. It is not fulfilling the requirements of faith and the covenant with Allah. But when the ummah succeeds in trial and passes the examination, or when it is afflicted with fear and seeks security from Allah; when it is humiliated and seeks honour from Allah; when it is left behind and seeks succession on earth, and does this with the means Allah has prescribed and under the conditions Allah has set, then Allah's promise, which is unalterable, is fulfilled. Then no power in the world can stand in the way of the Muslim ummah. This is why, after this promise, the command is given: establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And the believers and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should not be intimidated in the slightest by those disbelievers who are waging war against Allah, His Messenger and the religion of Islam.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verses 56–57:

(Wa aqimu al-salata ... wa labi'sa al-masir) (24:56–57)

These are the extremely brief conditions for preparation toward Allah: connection with Allah (ittisal billah), a bond with Allah, and setting the heart right through prayer (salah); and, through giving zakat, controlling the feelings of miserliness and love of wealth; obeying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the utmost willingness of heart; implementing Allah's commands in matters both small and great; and adopting the system of life that Allah has prescribed for living.

"La'allakum turhamun" (24:56): "So that you may be shown mercy." That is, it will save you in the earth from corruption, fear, restlessness and misguidance, and in the Hereafter it will save you from the wrath of Allah, the punishment of Allah and the vengeance of Allah.

When you set yourselves right according to this method, then there is no occasion for you to fear the strength of the disbelievers. They cannot overpower Allah and the people of Allah on the earth of Allah. Their apparent power cannot block your path, because your faith will be strong. You will have spiritual power as well. When you clash with disbelief as a believer, you will manifest strange and extraordinary miracles beyond the normal course of things.

In these verses, whoever wishes to benefit from the promise that Allah has made should develop within themselves this great reality of faith. In human history, one realization of this promise is certain, provided that the person who seeks its realization acts upon the conditions of the promise. Whenever these conditions are fulfilled, without any doubt and without any delay, this promise will be fulfilled.

Whenever the Muslim ummah has begun, or will begin, to walk on the path of Allah and the methodology of Allah, and whenever it has considered, or will consider, the Islamic system of life as the ruler of its life, and whenever the ummah has been, or will be, pleased with this religion, such that all its affairs conform to the Islamic system, then Allah's promise has been, and will be, realized. It has attained, and will attain, sovereign authority. Whenever the ummah has opposed these conditions, and will oppose them, it has been, and will be, humiliated. It has become, and will remain, a tail-follower of other nations. It has been, and will be, disgraced. It has been, and will be, removed from the position of leadership of the nations of the world. Fear has overtaken it, and will overtake it. Its enemies have seized it, and will seize it.

Beware! Know well that Allah's promise is true. Its conditions are known and clear. Whoever wishes may fulfil the conditions and test it, and none fulfils his promises more than Allah does.

**Lesson No. 156: A General Overview**

Islam is a complete system of life. It organizes the various aspects of human life. It brings order to all relationships, all contacts, all movements and rests, and all matters of human life. This is why Islam teaches the everyday etiquette of human life. Just as it teaches general duties and major affairs, it creates order and harmony in all these matters and turns all the affairs of life toward Allah.

This Surah is an excellent example of this. In this Surah, on the one hand, the laws and limits of Islam are set out. On the other hand, it teaches the etiquette of meeting among people living in one community, namely the law of *istidhan* (seeking permission to enter). Alongside this, it includes purely philosophical and scientific discussions on reflection over the whole universe. It also gives the lasting method for implementing the Islamic revolution: whenever you act upon it, sovereignty over the earth will be given to you. This lesson also teaches the etiquette of seeking permission when you go to someone's house to meet them. Then come the etiquette of the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then the etiquette of meeting, eating, drinking, hospitality, and benefiting from it, then the etiquette of speaking with one another and of speaking with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). All these etiquettes and guidances are related to the organization and training of the Islamic society. The fact is that the Holy Qur'an arranges the Islamic society in all matters, great and small.

**Lesson No. 156: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 58 to 64**

("O you who believe, let your slaves... and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." "And when the children reach... and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.")

In this Surah, the procedure for entering homes has already been discussed earlier, namely seeking permission before entering a house. Here, the discussion turns to those who may enter inside homes, or to those from whom the veil inside the home is not required, although the rules of seeking permission to enter still apply to them as well.

For example, servants, slaves, and boys who are not yet well acquainted with women's affairs may enter homes without restriction. However, they may not come in at three times when people take off their clothes and rest. At these specific times, these people too should enter only with permission. These times are: before the Fajr prayer, when people are usually in their sleeping clothes, or have not changed these clothes and have not put on their outdoor clothes; at noon, when people take a midday rest and, removing their usual clothing, rest; and after the Isha prayer, when everyone rests and is in their house clothes.

These times are called *awqat al-'awrat* (times of nakedness), meaning the times when people take off their clothes. At these times, domestic servants must be required to seek permission before going inside the house. Permission is also required for young boys who, although not yet mature, have reached the age of discernment, so that their eyes do not fall upon the bare bodies of the members of the household. These are etiquettes which, even in today's modern age, are not practiced in domestic life, and the psychological, nervous, and moral effects of not observing these restrictions are not taken seriously. People assume that the eyes of servants do not fall upon the masters of the house, and that boys before puberty are unaware of such matters. However, psychologists say that the scenes upon which children's eyes fall in childhood have an effect on their lives later on, and because of them they become afflicted with nervous and psychological illnesses for which there is no cure. It should be remembered that in our age, the science of psychology has progressed greatly. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware. He taught the believers these lofty etiquettes of this kind, because He wanted to create a nation whose nerves are sound and whole, whose chest is sound, whose consciousness is pure, whose hearts are clean, and whose thoughts are clear and pure.

These three times have been specified because during them people are generally in a state of carelessness, and, under the assumption that no outsider will come inside during these times, people do not bother to cover their bodies. If seeking permission had been made obligatory at all times for the domestic staff and young children, it would have caused great difficulty in practice, because servants and small children keep coming and going at all times.

Allah says: "Your going around to one another" (24:58), meaning that you constantly come and go among one another. Thus Allah has made arrangements for maintaining privacy, removed the difficulty, and also removed hardship and distress. If it had been made obligatory for them to seek permission at all times, just as with other unrelated adults, this would have caused you difficulties.

When young boys reach the age of puberty, they will come under the ruling of unrelated people, and they will fall under the same ruling that applies generally to people regarding seeking permission. Finally, it is said: "And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise" (24:58), because Allah alone knows the nature of human beings regarding the effects of legislation and moral conduct, and what is beneficial for them and what is not.

Earlier, a command was given that women should not display their adornment, so that no sexual temptation would enter the Islamic society. Here, elderly women who no longer have any desire for social interaction with men, and whose bodies no longer carry any such temptation, are exempted from that rule.

**Lesson No. 156: A General Overview**

Islam is a complete system of life. It organizes the various aspects of human life. It brings order to all relationships, all contacts, all movements and rests, and all matters of human life. This is why Islam teaches the everyday etiquette of human life. Just as it teaches general duties and major affairs, it creates order and harmony in all these matters and turns all the affairs of life toward Allah.

This Surah is an excellent example of this. In this Surah, on the one hand, the laws and limits of Islam are set out. On the other hand, it teaches the etiquette of meeting among people living in one community, namely the law of *istidhan* (seeking permission to enter). Alongside this, it includes purely philosophical and scientific discussions on reflection over the whole universe. It also gives the lasting method for implementing the Islamic revolution: whenever you act upon it, sovereignty over the earth will be given to you. This lesson also teaches the etiquette of seeking permission when you go to someone's house to meet them. Then come the etiquette of the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then the etiquette of meeting, eating, drinking, hospitality, and benefiting from it, then the etiquette of speaking with one another and of speaking with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). All these etiquettes and guidances are related to the organization and training of the Islamic society. The fact is that the Holy Qur'an arranges the Islamic society in all matters, great and small.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 60:

(And as for women past child-bearing... and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing) (60)

For those women who have passed the age of youth, if they lay aside their outer garments, there is no blame upon them. However, it is obligatory upon them too that they do not display their awrah (the parts of the body that must be covered) and do not display their adornment. Nevertheless, it is better for them too that they remain covered and keep wrapping themselves in their loose garments. This has been described as greater chastity (iffah), meaning it is more preferable for chastity and purity. For indeed, there is a close connection between tabarruj (display and ostentation), the display of adornment, and sexual temptation, and there is a close connection between hijab, veiling, and chastity and purity. This is the Islamic view of purity and chastity. In sum, Islam keeps veiled those matters that are sexually arousing to the beholder.

And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing (24:60): "Allah is the One who hears and sees." He hears and sees everything. He knows the things that are uttered by the tongue and also knows what passes through the hearts. The rulings of Islam rest upon intention and the awareness of conscience.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 61:

Now the rules concerning close relatives and friends

(Laysa... ta'qilun) (61) "It is reported in the narrations that people used to eat from the houses mentioned above. For this purpose they did not seek permission. They would also feed the poor, the blind, the lame and the sick along with themselves. Then people thought that permission had to be sought from the owners of the aforementioned houses as well. This thought arose in the hearts of the Muslims when this verse was revealed."

(Wa la ta'kulu amwalakum baynakum bil-batil) "And do not consume one another's property by false means." The believers were so sensitive that they constantly thought that they might violate the Qur'an. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse and gave them permission that they could eat from those houses. In this way, the blind, the lame and the sick poor were also exempted from the requirement of seeking the owners' permission to the extent of eating, and close relatives were given permission to eat, either alone or with these needy people, at their relative's home. These are situations in which the members of a household generally feed such people, and the common practice of people is that they eat and feed from such houses. However, in this matter the general principles of Islamic society will be observed, namely:

"There shall be no harm nor reciprocating harm" (la darar wa la dirar), and "It is not lawful for anyone to take the property of a Muslim except with his free consent" (la yahillu ma'mri'in muslimin illa bi-tibi nafs).

Since this is a legal verse, we shall discuss its manner of expression somewhat. The arrangement and composition of the phrases is such that the meaning comes clearly to mind. Also, the order of kinship has been kept in view. At the beginning, the houses of sons, husbands and wives are not mentioned explicitly, yet the subject is begun with them and they are expressed by the word "buyutikum" (your houses), because a son's house is his own house, a wife's house is her husband's house, and a husband's house is his wife's house. After this, the houses of forefathers are mentioned. After this, the houses of mother and maternal grandmother are mentioned. After this, the houses of brothers are mentioned. After this, the houses of sisters are mentioned. After this, the houses of paternal uncles are mentioned. After this, the houses of paternal aunts are mentioned. After this, the houses of maternal uncles are mentioned. After this, the houses of maternal aunts are mentioned, and after that the right of the person who is the keeper and supervisor of property is mentioned. For him it is permissible to eat from the property under his supervision to the extent of need. Along with this, the house of friends is also mentioned: a friend may eat from the house of a friend, provided that it does not become a cause of distress or harm to the friend, because often friends eat and drink in each other's houses without permission.

Now, after describing the houses in which eating is permitted, it is also explained in what state the eating should take place.

(Laysa... ashtatan) (24:61) "There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately." Among some Arabs, in the days of ignorance, it was the custom that none of them would eat without a companion. If no guest or companion was available, they would not eat at all. Allah abolished this custom, since sometimes it caused difficulties. He made the matter easy: whether one eats alone or with others, both situations are appropriate.

After describing the houses and the manner of eating, here it is explained how to enter the houses in which eating has been permitted.

(Fa-idha... mubarakatan tayyibah) (24:61) "But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good." This is a most subtle expression of the strong bond that exists among the aforementioned relationships. That is, greet your own selves, for one who greets his relatives or friends in fact sends peace upon himself, and the greeting he gives is from Allah. Within the greeting there is a spiritual breath from Allah, and between both parties there is a firm bond of religion, the religious bond which is established through the greeting. This is an extremely unbreakable bond.

(Kadhalika... ta'qilun) (24:61) "Thus Allah makes the verses clear to you, that you may understand." You should know how much wisdom has been kept in view in the system of life ordained by Allah, and how appropriate and balanced that system is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 62:

(Innamal-mu'minoona alladheena... Ghafoorun Raheem. La taj'aloo du'a'a'ir-Rasooli baynakum ka-du'a'i ba'dikum ba'dan... Wallahu bikulli shay'in 'Aleem.) (24:62-64)

Ibn Ishaq has narrated the following report regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse: at the time of the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab), when the Quraysh gathered all the tribes and marched upon Madinah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the digging of a trench (khandaq) around Madinah for its defence. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself also took part in digging the trench so that the believers would work with enthusiasm. The Muslims worked in the digging of the trench with great zeal. He set an example and a model, and they too set an example. Some of the hypocrites (munafiqeen) showed a tendency to lag behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims in this work and to act sluggishly. They would make excuses for minor and major tasks and slip away, and some would leave without seeking permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whereas the practice of the Muslims was that when they had some necessary business, they would mention it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He (ﷺ) would grant permission, and that person would complete the task and quickly return to the work. And Muslims adopted this conduct in order to earn greater reward. On this occasion, Allah revealed these verses.

Whatever the occasion of revelation, from "Innamal-mu'minoon" to the end, the verses mention the organisational rules and etiquettes of the community of Muslims, and etiquettes concerning the commands of the leader of the Muslims are described. Unless a community observes such principles with deep feeling and from the depths of its conscience, the order and administration of the community cannot be correct. These etiquettes should continue within the community of Muslims as a firm tradition, an accepted habit and a strict law. If this does not happen, that group will not be a community but a mob of scattered individuals.

(Wa idha... yasta'dhinoohu) (24:62): "And when they are with him on a matter requiring assembly, they do not depart until they have asked his permission." The "matter requiring assembly" (amr jami') refers to a matter in which the participation of the whole community of Muslims is necessary. Whether it is an occasion of consultation, or of war, or of general communal work, on such occasions it is the duty of believers to depart only after taking permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). After him, they should take permission from their imam and their in-charge, so that the life of Muslims and their institutions may function in an organised manner, there may be no disorder among them, and every task may be carried out with discipline and dignity.

Those who believe in this manner and then act upon these etiquettes, and seek release from the duty of the movement only when they are compelled, do not flee from their duty because of their faith and their training, even when the ummah and the community are in dire need of collective struggle. But the Qur'an gives the Prophet (ﷺ) the authority to decide whether to grant permission or not. After him, this authority now belongs to the head of the community, to decide whether he exempts someone from communal tasks or not.

(Fa idha... minhum) (24:62): "So when they ask you for permission for some of their affairs, grant permission to whomever you wish of them." Before this, Allah had admonished the Prophet (ﷺ) that why he had granted permission to those hypocrites: "Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them permission until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?" (9:43 style rendering) Here, the matter is left to the discernment of the Prophet (ﷺ), whether he grants permission to someone or not. In this way, another ease has been created for Muslims, because at times extremely important needs arise; therefore the leadership of the community has been given the authority to weigh whether it is necessary for someone to go on a pressing campaign or to remain behind for a special need. The final authority has been given to the leader so that he may decide while keeping circumstances in view.

Here, however, it is indicated that individual needs should be controlled, solutions should be found for problems, and the collective mission should be given preference. Nevertheless, if a person stays behind even for a lawful need of his own, then despite its being permissible, it is still a fault, and it is necessary for him to seek forgiveness from Allah.

(Wastaghfir lahumullah inna Allaha Ghafoorun Raheem) (24:62): "And ask forgiveness of Allah for them; indeed Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Thus a restraint is placed on the conscience of the believer, that he should not seek permission, and if any situation arises, he should try to save himself from having to seek excuses.

Furthermore, it is also mentioned here that those who seek permission should present their request in very respectful words, and should not address him in the manner of the common people, such as "Ya Muhammad" or "Ya Aba al-Qasim" or in another ordinary manner; rather they should address him with respectful words such as "Ya Rasool Allah" or "Ya Nabi Allah".

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 24, verse 63:

﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like the calling of some of you to others.﴾ (24:63) O Muslims, do not consider the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves to be the same as one of you calling another. It is proper that your hearts be filled with love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore, in showing respect to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), choose the most fitting words. This is an extremely essential principle for leadership, because the proper respect of a trainer, a teacher, or a leader is necessary, and in the consciousness and conduct of the workers there should be respect and love. A worker should not be excessively informal with his leader. After this, the hypocrites are warned that they slip away without the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they flee by taking cover behind one another. If they hide themselves from the sight of the Muslims and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they certainly cannot hide from the sight of Allah.

﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, taking cover behind one another.﴾ (24:63) This is a strange portrayal of a person who slips away from the gathering unseen, concealing himself from its view. Its purpose is to show that such a person does not leave openly with permission, but exits like a thief, hiding himself, and this conduct creates contempt for that person within consciousness.

﴿So let those who oppose his order beware lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment afflict them.﴾ (24:63) Those who oppose the command of the Messenger should be wary that they may not be seized by some trial, or those who oppose his affair, who follow ways contrary to the methods of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and who slip away quietly from the ranks of the collective teams for personal affairs and personal interests. They should fear that differences may arise among them and they may be afflicted with a great trial. Lest their values themselves change, the distinction between truth and falsehood be lost, and their system become unsteady. Lest the pure and the impure become mixed among them, disorder set in within communal affairs, and the joints of communal life become loose. In such a way that no person is content with regard to his own self, no one stops at any limit, and the standard of good and evil disappears from within the community. Such conditions are harmful for all members of the community.

﴿Or a painful punishment afflict them.﴾ (24:63) Whether this punishment comes in this world or in the Hereafter. This punishment will come because these people opposed the command of Allah and abandoned the system that Allah had chosen for them.

Here this warning and intense fear ends. With it Surah an-Nur also ends, and at the conclusion of the discourse people are cautioned that Allah is aware of all your deeds. He knows those who do good deeds and He knows those who have set out on paths of deviation, and one day He will present to you your complete record of deeds.

The verse is cited in the passage as: (Verily, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth... and He has knowledge of everything) (24:63).

Thus this surah concludes on the theme that the eyes of the believers are turned toward Allah, and they are warned with the fear and awe of Allah, because God alone, the awe of God, and taqwa (God-consciousness) are the final guarantee for keeping a person upright. This is the ultimate overseer of implementing the commands and prohibitions that Allah has given, which sits in the heart of every believer. The morals, etiquette and laws that have been established in this surah, and which have all been made an equal part of the Islamic system, have been declared to be guarded by taqwa and fear of God.
